Previously, inputs to [json_decode()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.json-decode.php) that consisted solely of one of these values in upper or mixed case were accepted.

This change will only affect cases where invalid JSON was being passed to [json_decode()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.json-decode.php): valid JSON input is unaffected and will continue to be parsed normally.

### Stream wrappers now verify peer certificates and host names by default when using SSL/TLS

All encrypted client streams now enable peer verification by default. By default, this will use OpenSSL's default CA bundle to verify the peer certificate. In most cases, no changes will need to be made to communicate with servers with valid SSL certificates, as distributors generally configure OpenSSL to use known good CA bundles.

The default CA bundle may be overridden on a global basis by setting either the openssl.cafile or openssl.capath configuration setting, or on a per request basis by using the [`cafile`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.cafile) or [`capath`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.capath) context options.

While not recommended in general, it is possible to disable peer certificate verification for a request by setting the [`verify_peer`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.verify-peer) context option to **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)**, and to disable peer name validation by setting the [`verify_peer_name`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.verify-peer-name) context option to **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)**.

### [GMP](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.gmp.php) resources are now objects

[GMP](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.gmp.php) resources are now objects. The functional API implemented in the GMP extension has not changed, and code should run unmodified unless it checks explicitly for a resource using [is_resource()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-resource.php) or similar.

### [Mcrypt](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.mcrypt.php) functions now require valid keys and IVs

[mcrypt_encrypt()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mcrypt-encrypt.php), [mcrypt_decrypt()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mcrypt-decrypt.php), **mcrypt_cbc()**, **mcrypt_cfb()**, **mcrypt_ecb()**, [mcrypt_generic()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mcrypt-generic.php) and **mcrypt_ofb()** will no longer accept keys or IVs with incorrect sizes, and block cipher modes that require IVs will now fail if an IV isn't provided.

### [cURL](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.curl.php) file uploads

Uploads using the @file syntax now require CURLOPT_SAFE_UPLOAD to be set to **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)**. [CURLFile](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.curlfile.php) should be used instead.

# [PHP 5.5](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration55.incompatible.php)

## Backward Incompatible Changes

Although most existing PHP 5 code should work without changes, please take note of some backward incompatible changes:

### Windows XP and 2003 support dropped

Support for Windows XP and 2003 has been dropped. Windows builds of PHP now require Windows Vista or newer.

### Case insensitivity no longer locale specific

All case insensitive matching for function, class and constant names is now performed in a locale independent manner according to ASCII rules. This improves support for languages using the Latin alphabet with unusual collating rules, such as Turkish and Azeri.

This may cause issues for code that uses case insensitive matches for non-ASCII characters in multibyte character sets (including UTF-8), such as accented characters in many European languages. If you have a non-English, non-ASCII code base, then you will need to test that you are not inadvertently relying on this behaviour before deploying PHP 5.5 to production systems.

### [pack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.pack.html) and [unpack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.unpack.html) changes

Changes were made to [pack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.pack.html) and [unpack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.unpack.html) to make them more compatible with Perl:

- [pack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.pack.html) now supports the "Z" format code, which behaves identically to "a".
- [unpack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.unpack.html) now support the "Z" format code for NULL padded strings, and behaves as "a" did in previous versions: it will strip trailing NULL bytes.
- [unpack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.unpack.html) now keeps trailing NULL bytes when the "a" format code is used.
- [unpack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.unpack.html) now strips all trailing ASCII whitespace when the "A" format code is used.

Writing backward compatible code that uses the "a" format code with [unpack()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.unpack.html) requires the use of [version_compare()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.version-compare.html), due to the backward compatibility break.

For example:

    <?php
    // Old code:
    $data = unpack('a5', $packed);

    // New code:
    if (version_compare(PHP_VERSION, '5.5.0-dev', '>=')) {
      $data = unpack('Z5', $packed);
    } else {
      $data = unpack('a5', $packed);
    }
    ?>

### [json_encode()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.json-encode.html) changes

When the `value` passed to [json_encode()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.json-encode.html) triggers a JSON encoding error, **`FALSE`** is returned instead of partial output, unless `options` contains **`JSON_PARTIAL_OUTPUT_ON_ERROR`**. See [json_last_error()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.json-last-error.html) for the full list of reasons that can cause JSON encoding to fail. One of the potential failure reasons is that `value` contains strings containing invalid UTF-8.

### `self`, `parent` and `static` are now always case insensitive

Prior to PHP 5.5, cases existed where the [self](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.paamayim-nekudotayim.html), [parent](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.paamayim-nekudotayim.html), and [static](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.late-static-bindings.html) keywords were treated in a case sensitive fashion. These have now been resolved, and these keywords are always handled case insensitively: `SELF::CONSTANT` is now treated identically to `self::CONSTANT`.

### PHP logo GUIDs removed

The GUIDs that previously resulted in PHP outputting various logos have been removed. This includes the removal of the functions to return those GUIDs. The removed functions are:

- [php_logo_guid()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.php-logo-guid.html)
- **php_egg_logo_guid()**
- **php_real_logo_guid()**
- [zend_logo_guid()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.zend-logo-guid.html)

### Internal execution changes

Extension authors should note that the **zend_execute()** function can no longer be overridden, and that numerous changes have been made to the `execute_data` struct and related function and method handling opcodes.

Most extension authors are unlikely to be affected, but those writing extensions that hook deeply into the Zend Engine should read [the notes on these changes](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration55.internals.html).

# [PHP 5.4](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration54.incompatible.php)

## Backward Incompatible Changes

Although most existing PHP 5 code should work without changes, please take note of some backward incompatible changes:

- [Safe mode](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/features.safe-mode.html) is no longer supported. Any applications that rely on safe mode may need adjustment, in terms of security.
- [Magic quotes](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/security.magicquotes.html) has been removed. Applications relying on this feature may need to be updated, to avoid security issues. [get_magic_quotes_gpc()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-magic-quotes-gpc.html) and [get_magic_quotes_runtime()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-magic-quotes-runtime.html) now always return **`FALSE`**. [set_magic_quotes_runtime()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.set-magic-quotes-runtime.html) raises an **`E_CORE_ERROR`** level error on trying to enable [Magic quotes](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/security.magicquotes.html).
- The [register_globals](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.register-globals) and [register_long_arrays](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.register-long-arrays) `php.ini` directives have been removed.
- The mbstring.script_encoding directive has been removed. Use [zend.script_encoding](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend.script-encoding) instead.
- [Call-time pass by reference](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.references.pass.html) has been removed.
- The [break](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/control-structures.break.html) and [continue](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/control-structures.continue.html) statements no longer accept variable arguments (e.g., `break 1 + foo() * $bar;`). Static arguments still work, such as `break 2;`. As a side effect of this change `break 0;` and `continue 0;` are no longer allowed.
- The default character set for [htmlspecialchars()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlspecialchars.html), [htmlentities()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlentities.html) and [html_entity_decode()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.html-entity-decode.html) is now `UTF-8`, instead of `ISO-8859-1`. Note that changing your output charset via the [default_charset](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.default-charset) configuration setting does not affect htmlspecialchars/htmlentities unless you are passing "" (an empty string) as the encoding parameter to your [htmlspecialchars()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlspecialchars.html)/[htmlentities()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlentities.html)/[html_entity_decode()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.html-entity-decode.html) calls. Generally we do not recommend doing this because you should be able to change your output charset without affecting the runtime charset used by these functions. The safest approach is to explicitly set the charset on each call to [htmlspecialchars()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlspecialchars.html), [htmlentities()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlentities.html) and [html_entity_decode()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.html-entity-decode.html).
- In the [date and time extension](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.datetime.html), the timezone can no longer be set using the TZ environment variable. Instead you have to specify a timezone using the [date.timezone](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/datetime.configuration.html#ini.date.timezone) `php.ini` option or [date_default_timezone_set()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-default-timezone-set.html) function. PHP will no longer attempt to guess the timezone, and will instead fall back to "UTC" and issue a **`E_WARNING`**.
- Non-numeric string offsets - e.g. `$a['foo']` where \$a is a string - now return false on [isset()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.isset.html) and true on [empty()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.empty.html), and produce a **`E_WARNING`** if you try to use them. Offsets of types double, bool and null produce a **`E_NOTICE`**. Numeric strings (e.g. `$a['2']`) still work as before. Note that offsets like `'12.3'` and `'5 foobar'` are considered non-numeric and produce a **`E_WARNING`**, but are converted to 12 and 5 respectively, for backward compatibility reasons. Note: Following code returns different result. \$str='abc';var_dump(isset(\$str\['x'\])); // false for PHP 5.4 or later, but true for 5.3 or less
- Converting an array to a string will now generate an **`E_NOTICE`** level error, but the result of the cast will still be the string `"Array"`.
- Turning **`NULL`**, **`FALSE`**, or an empty string into an object by adding a property will now emit an **`E_WARNING`** level error, instead of **`E_STRICT`**.
- Parameter names that shadow super globals now cause a fatal error. This prohibits code like `function foo($_GET, $_POST) {}`.
- The Salsa10 and Salsa20 [hash algorithms](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.hash.html) have been removed.
- The Tiger [hash algorithm](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.hash.html) now uses big-endian byte ordering. Please follow [this example](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.hash.html#function.hash.tiger-bc) to write code that is compatible with both PHP 5.3 and 5.4.
- [array_combine()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-combine.html) now returns `array()` instead of **`FALSE`** when two empty arrays are provided as parameters.
- If you use [htmlentities()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlentities.html) with asian character sets, it works like [htmlspecialchars()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.htmlspecialchars.html) - this has always been the case in previous versions of PHP, but now an **`E_STRICT`** level error is emitted.
- The third parameter of [ob_start()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.ob-start.html) has changed from [boolean](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.types.boolean.html) `erase` to [integer](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.types.integer.html) `flags`. Note that code that explicitly set `erase` to **`FALSE`** will no longer behave as expected in PHP 5.4: please follow [this example](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.ob-start.html#function.ob-start.flags-bc) to write code that is compatible with PHP 5.3 and 5.4.

The following keywords are now [reserved](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.html), and may not be used as names by functions, classes, etc.

- [trait](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.traits.html)
- [callable](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.types.callable.html)
- [insteadof](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.traits.html)

The following functions have been removed from PHP:

- [define_syslog_variables()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.define-syslog-variables.html)
- [import_request_variables()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.import-request-variables.html)
- [session_is_registered()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.session-is-registered.html), [session_register()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.session-register.html) and [session_unregister()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.session-unregister.html).
- The aliases [mysqli_bind_param()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysqli-bind-param.html), [mysqli_bind_result()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysqli-bind-result.html), [mysqli_client_encoding()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysqli-client-encoding.html), [mysqli_fetch()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysqli-fetch.html), [mysqli_param_count()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysqli-param-count.html), [mysqli_get_metadata()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysqli-get-metadata.html), [mysqli_send_long_data()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysqli-send-long-data.html), mysqli::client_encoding() and mysqli_stmt::stmt().

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.incompatible.php)

## Backward Incompatible Changes

Although most existing PHP 5 code should work without changes, please take note of some backward incompatible changes:

- The newer internal parameter parsing API has been applied across all the extensions bundled with PHP 5.3.x. This parameter parsing API causes functions to return **`NULL`** when passed incompatible parameters. There are some exceptions to this rule, such as the [get_class()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-class.html) function, which will continue to return **`FALSE`** on error.
- [clearstatcache()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.clearstatcache.html) no longer clears the realpath cache by default.
- [realpath()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.realpath.html) is now fully platform-independent. Consequence of this is that invalid relative paths such as `__FILE__ . "/../x"` do not work anymore.
- The [call_user_func()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.call-user-func.html) family of functions now propagate `$this` even if the callee is a parent class.
- The array functions [natsort()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.natsort.html), [natcasesort()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.natcasesort.html), [usort()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.usort.html), [uasort()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.uasort.html), [uksort()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.uksort.html), [array_flip()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-flip.html), and [array_unique()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-unique.html) no longer accept objects passed as arguments. To apply these functions to an object, cast the object to an array first.
- The behaviour of functions with by-reference parameters called by value has changed. Where previously the function would accept the by-value argument, a fatal error is now emitted. Any previous code passing constants or literals to functions expecting references, will need altering to assign the value to a variable before calling the function.
- The new mysqlnd library necessitates the use of MySQL 4.1's newer 41-byte password format. Continued use of the old 16-byte passwords will cause [mysql_connect()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mysql-connect.html) and similar functions to emit the error, `"mysqlnd cannot connect to MySQL 4.1+ using old authentication."`
- The new mysqlnd library does not read mysql configuration files (my.cnf/my.ini), as the older libmysqlclient library does. If your code relies on settings in the configuration file, you can load it explicitly with the [mysqli_options()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/mysqli.options.html) function. Note that this means the PDO specific constants **`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_READ_DEFAULT_FILE`** and **`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_READ_DEFAULT_GROUP`** are not defined if MySQL support in PDO is compiled with mysqlnd.
- The trailing / has been removed from the [SplFileInfo](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.splfileinfo.html) class and other related directory classes.
- The [\_\_toString()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.magic.html#object.tostring) magic method can no longer accept arguments.
- The magic methods [\_\_get()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.overloading.html#object.get), [\_\_set()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.overloading.html#object.set), [\_\_isset()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.overloading.html#object.isset), [\_\_unset()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.overloading.html#object.unset), and [\_\_call()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.overloading.html#object.call) must always be public and can no longer be static. Method signatures are now enforced.
- The [\_\_call()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.overloading.html#object.call) magic method is now invoked on access to private and protected methods.
- [func_get_arg()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.func-get-arg.html), [func_get_args()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.func-get-args.html) and [func_num_args()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.func-num-args.html) can no longer be called from the outermost scope of a file that has been included by calling [include](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.include.html) or [require](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.require.html) from within a function in the calling file.
- An emulation layer for the MHASH extension to wrap around the Hash extension have been added. However not all the algorithms are covered, notable the s2k hashing algorithm. This means that s2k hashing is no longer available as of PHP 5.3.0.

The following keywords are now reserved and may not be used in function, class, etc. names.

- [goto](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/control-structures.goto.html)
- [namespace](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.namespaces.html)

# [PHP 5.2](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration52.incompatible.php)

## Backward Incompatible Changes

Although most existing PHP 5 code should work without changes, you should pay attention to the following backward incompatible changes:

- [getrusage()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.getrusage.html) returns **`NULL`** when passed incompatible arguments as of PHP 5.2.1.

- [ZipArchive::setCommentName()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ziparchive.setcommentname.html) returns **`TRUE`** on success as of PHP 5.2.1.

- [ZipArchive::setCommentIndex()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ziparchive.setcommentindex.html) returns **`TRUE`** on success as of PHP 5.2.1.

- **SplFileObject::getFilename()** returns the filename, not relative/path/to/file, as of PHP 5.2.1.

- Changed priority of `PHPRC` environment variable on Win32 The `PHPRC` environment variable now takes priority over the path stored in the Windows registry.

- CLI SAPI no longer checks cwd for `php.ini` or the `php-cli.ini` file In PHP 5.1.x an undocumented feature was added that made the CLI binary check the current working directory for a PHP configuration file, potentially leading to unpredictable behavior if an unexpected configuration file were read. This functionality was removed in 5.2.0, and PHP will no longer search CWD for the presence of `php.ini` or `php-cli.ini` files. See also the [command line](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/features.commandline.html) section of the manual.

- Added a warning when performing modulus 0 operations In earlier versions of PHP, performing integer % 0 did not emit any warning messages, instead returning an unexpected return value of **`FALSE`**. As of PHP 5.2.0, this operation will emit an **`E_WARNING`**, as is the case in all other instances where division by zero is performed.

      <?php
      print 10 % 0;
      /* Warning:  Division by zero in filename on line n */
      ?>

- Changed [\_\_toString()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.magic.html#object.tostring) to be called wherever applicable. The magic method [\_\_toString()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.magic.html#object.tostring) will now be called in a string context, that is, anywhere an object is used as a string. The fallback of returning a string that contains the object identifier was dropped in PHP 5.2.0. It became problematic because an object identifier cannot be considered unique. This change will mean that your application is flawed if you have relied on the object identifier as a return value. An attempt to use that value as a string will now result in a catchable fatal error.

      <?php
      class foo {}
      $foo = new foo;
      print $foo;
      /* Catchable fatal error:  Object of class foo could
         not be converted to string in filename on line n */
      ?>

  Even with [\_\_toString()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.magic.html#object.tostring), objects cannot be used as array indices or keys. We may add built-in hash support for this at a later date, but as of PHP 5.2.x you will need to either provide your own hashing or use the new SPL function [spl_object_hash()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.spl-object-hash.html). Exceptions can not be thrown from [\_\_toString()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.magic.html#object.tostring) methods.

      <?php
      class foo {
          public function __toString() {
              throw new Exception;
          }
      }

      try {
          print new foo;
          /* Fatal error:  Method foo::__toString() must
             not throw an exception in filename on line n */
      } catch(Exception $e) {}
      ?>

- Dropped abstract static class functions. Due to an oversight, PHP 5.0.x and 5.1.x allowed abstract static functions in classes. As of PHP 5.2.x, only interfaces can have them.

      <?php
      abstract class foo {
          abstract static function bar();
          /* Strict Standards:  Static function foo::bar()
             should not be abstract in filename on line n */
      }
      ?>

- [Oracle extension](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.oci8.html) requires at least Oracle 10 on Windows.

- Added RFC2397 (`data:` stream) support. The introduction of the 'data' URL scheme has the potential to lead to a change of behavior under Windows. If you are working with a NTFS file system and making use of meta streams in your application, and if you just happen to be using a file with the name 'data:' that is accessed without any path information - it won't work any more. The fix is to use the 'file:' protocol when accessing it. See also [» RFC 2397](http://www.faqs.org/rfcs/rfc2397)

      <?php
      /* when allow_url_include is OFF (default) */
      include "data:;base64,PD9waHAgcGhwaW5mbygpOz8+";
      /* Warning:  include(): URL file-access is disabled
         in the server configuration in filename on line n */
      ?>

- Regression in `glob()` patterns In version 5.2.4 a security fix caused a regression for patterns of the form "/foo/\*/bar/\*". Since version 5.2.5 instead of raising a warning the `glob()` function will return **`FALSE`** when `openbase_dir` restrictions are violated.

# [PHP 5.0](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.incompatible.php)

## Backward Incompatible Changes

Although most existing PHP 4 code should work without changes, you should pay attention to the following backward incompatible changes:

- There are some [new reserved keywords](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.keywords.html).
- [strrpos()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.strrpos.html) and [strripos()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.strripos.html) now use the entire string as a needle.
- Illegal use of string offsets causes **`E_ERROR`** instead of **`E_WARNING`**. An example illegal use is: `$str = 'abc'; unset($str[0]);`.
- [array_merge()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-merge.html) was changed to accept only arrays. If a non-array variable is passed, a **`E_WARNING`** will be thrown for every such parameter. Be careful because your code may start emitting **`E_WARNING`** out of the blue.
- **`PATH_TRANSLATED`** server variable is no longer set implicitly under Apache2 SAPI in contrast to the situation in PHP 4, where it is set to the same value as the **`SCRIPT_FILENAME`** server variable when it is not populated by Apache. This change was made to comply with the [» CGI/1.1 specification](http://www.faqs.org/rfcs/rfc3875). Please refer to [» bug \#23610](https://bugs.php.net/23610) for further information, and see also the [`$_SERVER['PATH_TRANSLATED']`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.server.html) description in the manual. This issue also affects PHP versions \>= 4.3.2.
- The **`T_ML_COMMENT`** constant is no longer defined by the [Tokenizer](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.tokenizer.html) extension. If error_reporting is set to **`E_ALL`**, PHP will generate a notice. Although the **`T_ML_COMMENT`** was never used at all, it was defined in PHP 4. In both PHP 4 and PHP 5 // and /\* \*/ are resolved as the **`T_COMMENT`** constant. However the PHPDoc style comments `/** */`, which starting PHP 5 are parsed by PHP, are recognized as **`T_DOC_COMMENT`**.
- [`$_SERVER`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.server.html) should be populated with `argc` and `argv` if [variables_order](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.variables-order) includes "S". If you have specifically configured your system to not create [`$_SERVER`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.server.html), then of course it shouldn't be there. The change was to always make `argc` and `argv` available in the CLI version regardless of the [variables_order](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.variables-order) setting. As in, the CLI version will now always populate the global [`$argc`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.argc.html) and [`$argv`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.argv.html) variables.
- An object with no properties is no longer considered "empty".
- In some cases classes must be declared before use. It only happens if some of the new features of PHP 5 (such as [interfaces](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.interfaces.html)) are used. Otherwise the behaviour is the old.
- [get_class()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-class.html), [get_parent_class()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-parent-class.html) and [get_class_methods()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-class-methods.html) now return the name of the classes/methods as they were declared (case-sensitive) which may lead to problems in older scripts that rely on the previous behaviour (the class/method name was always returned lowercased). A possible solution is to search for those functions in all your scripts and use [strtolower()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.strtolower.html). This case sensitivity change also applies to the [magical predefined constants](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.constants.predefined.html) **`__CLASS__`**, **`__METHOD__`**, and **`__FUNCTION__`**. The values are returned exactly as they're declared (case-sensitive).
- [ip2long()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.ip2long.html) now returns **`FALSE`** when an invalid IP address is passed as argument to the function, and no longer `-1`.
- If there are functions defined in the included file, they can be used in the main file independent if they are before [return](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.return.html) or after. If the file is included twice, PHP 5 issues fatal error because functions were already declared, while PHP 4 doesn't complain about it. It is recommended to use [include_once](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.include-once.html) instead of checking if the file was already included and conditionally return inside the included file.
- [include_once](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.include-once.html) and [require_once](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.require-once.html) first normalize the path of included file on Windows so that including A.php and a.php include the file just once.
- Passing an array to a function by value no longer resets the array's internal pointer for array accesses made within the function. In other words, in PHP 4 when you passed an array to a function, its internal pointer inside the function would be reset, while in PHP 5, when you pass an array to a function, its array pointer within the function will be wherever it was when the array was passed to the function.

**Example \#1 [strrpos()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.strrpos.html) and [strripos()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.strripos.html) now use the entire string as a needle**

    <?php
    var_dump(strrpos('ABCDEF','DEF')); //int(3)

    var_dump(strrpos('ABCDEF','DAF')); //bool(false)
    ?>

**Example \#2 An object with no properties is no longer considered "empty"**

    <?php
    class test { }
    $t = new test();

    var_dump(empty($t)); // echo bool(false)

    if ($t) {
        // Will be executed
    }
    ?>

**Example \#3 In some cases classes must be declared before used**

    <?php

    //works with no errors:
    $a = new a();
    class a {
    }


    //throws an error:
    $a = new b();

    interface c{
    }
    class b implements c {
    } 

    ?>

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.functions.php)

## New Functions

PHP 5.3 introduced some new functions:

PHP Core:

- [array_replace()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-replace.html) - Replaces elements from passed arrays into one array.
- [array_replace_recursive()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-replace-recursive.html) - Recursively replaces elements from passed arrays into one array.
- [class_alias()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.class-alias.html) - Creates an alias for a user defined class.
- [forward_static_call()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.forward-static-call.html) - Call a user function from a method context.
- [forward_static_call_array()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.forward-static-call-array.html) - Call a user function from a method context, with the arguments contained in an array.
- [gc_collect_cycles()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.gc-collect-cycles.html) - Forces collection of any existing garbage cycles.
- [gc_disable()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.gc-disable.html) - Deactivates the circular reference collector.
- [gc_enable()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.gc-enable.html) - Activates the circular reference collector.
- [gc_enabled()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.gc-enabled.html) - Returns the status of the circular reference collector.
- [get_called_class()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-called-class.html) - Return the name of the class a static method is called in.
- [gethostname()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.gethostname.html) - Return the current host name for the local machine.
- [header_remove()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.header-remove.html) - Removes an HTTP header previously set using the [header()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.header.html) function.
- [lcfirst()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.lcfirst.html) - Make a string's first character lowercase.
- [parse_ini_string()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.parse-ini-string.html) - Parse a configuration string.
- [quoted_printable_encode()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.quoted-printable-encode.html) - Convert an 8 bit string to a quoted-printable string.
- [str_getcsv()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.str-getcsv.html) - Parse a CSV string into an array.
- [stream_context_set_default()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.stream-context-set-default.html) - Set the default stream context.
- [stream_supports_lock()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.stream-supports-lock.html) - Return **`TRUE`** if the stream supports locking.
- [stream_context_get_params()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.stream-context-get-params.html) - Retrieve parameters from a stream context.
- [streamWrapper::stream_cast()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/streamwrapper.stream-cast.html) - Retrieve the underlying stream resource.
- [streamWrapper::stream_set_option()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/streamwrapper.stream-set-option.html) - Change stream options

[Date/Time](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.datetime.html):

- [date_add()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-add.html) - Adds an amount of days, months, years, hours, minutes and seconds to a [DateTime](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.datetime.html) object.
- [date_create_from_format()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-create-from-format.html) - Returns a new [DateTime](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.datetime.html) object formatted according to the given format.
- [date_diff()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-diff.html) - Returns the difference between two [DateTime](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.datetime.html) objects.
- [date_get_last_errors()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-get-last-errors.html) - Returns the warnings and errors from the last date/time operation.
- [date_parse_from_format()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-parse-from-format.html) - Get information about a given date.
- [date_sub()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-sub.html) - Subtracts an amount of days, months, years, hours, minutes and seconds from a [DateTime](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.datetime.html) object.
- [timezone_version_get()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.timezone-version-get.html) - Returns the version of the timezonedb.

[GMP](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.gmp.html):

# [PHP 5.0](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.functions.php)

## New Functions

In PHP 5 there are some new functions. Here is the list of them:

[Arrays](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.array.html):

- [array_combine()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-combine.html) - Creates an array by using one array for keys and another for its values
- [array_diff_uassoc()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-diff-uassoc.html) - Computes the difference of arrays with additional index check which is performed by a user supplied callback function
- [array_udiff()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-udiff.html) - Computes the difference of arrays by using a callback function for data comparison
- [array_udiff_assoc()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-udiff-assoc.html) - Computes the difference of arrays with additional index check. The data is compared by using a callback function
- [array_udiff_uassoc()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-udiff-uassoc.html) - Computes the difference of arrays with additional index check. The data is compared by using a callback function. The index check is done by a callback function also
- [array_walk_recursive()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-walk-recursive.html) - Apply a user function recursively to every member of an array
- [array_uintersect_assoc()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-uintersect-assoc.html) - Computes the intersection of arrays with additional index check. The data is compared by using a callback function
- [array_uintersect_uassoc()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-uintersect-uassoc.html) - Computes the intersection of arrays with additional index check. Both the data and the indexes are compared by using separate callback functions
- [array_uintersect()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-uintersect.html) - Computes the intersection of arrays. The data is compared by using a callback function

# [Deprecated Features in PHP 8.6, 8.5, 8.4, 8.3, 8.2, 8.1, 8.0, 7.4, 7.3, 7.2, 7.1, 7.0, 5.6, 5.5, 5.4, 5.3](index.md)

# [PHP 8.6](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration86.deprecated.php)

## Deprecated Features

### PHP Core

#### Using "namespace" as a class constant name

Declaring a [class constant](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.constants.php) named `namespace` is now deprecated. `namespace` is a semi-reserved keyword, and the name is being reserved for possible future syntax such as a `::namespace` pseudo-constant analogous to `::class`. Methods and static properties named `namespace` are not affected. Rename the constant, for example to `NAMESPACE_NAME`.

#### Returning from a finally block

Using the `return` statement inside a [`finally`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/control-structures.finally.php) block is now deprecated, and emits a compile-time deprecation notice. Such a `return` silently discards an exception thrown by, or overwrites the value returned from, the associated `try` or `catch` block, so failures vanish without a trace. Move the `return` out of the `finally` block instead; the same result can always be expressed without it.

```
<?php
function getConfig(): array
{
    try {
        return loadConfig(); // throws if the file is missing
    } finally {
        return []; // Deprecated: the exception is gone, the caller just gets []
    }
}
```

#### Nullable return type for \_\_debugInfo()

Declaring a return type of ?[array](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.array.php) for [\_\_debugInfo()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.magic.php#language.oop5.magic.debuginfo) is now deprecated. Returning **[`null`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.null)** from this method was [already deprecated in PHP 8.5](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration85.deprecated.php#migration85.deprecated.core.return-null-from-debuginfo), so the nullable return type no longer describes valid behaviour. Declare [array](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.array.php) instead.

#### Returning values from \_\_construct() and \_\_destruct()

Returning a value from [\_\_construct()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.decon.php#language.oop5.decon.constructor) or [\_\_destruct()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.decon.php#language.oop5.decon.destructor) is now deprecated, and emits a compile-time deprecation notice. These methods cannot declare a return type, and their return value can never be observed during normal use, which made returning a value confusing at best. Using `return;` without a value to skip the remaining logic is still allowed, as is calling these methods manually.

For the same reason, using `yield` to make [\_\_construct()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.decon.php#language.oop5.decon.constructor) or [\_\_destruct()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.decon.php#language.oop5.decon.destructor) a [generator](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.generators.php) is now deprecated.

#### Naming a function readonly

Declaring a function named `readonly` is now deprecated. [readonly](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.properties.php#language.oop5.properties.readonly-properties) is a reserved keyword; a lexer exception was added in PHP 8.1 solely to keep an existing WordPress function of that name working, and no other keyword in PHP receives such special treatment. Rename the function.

#### Using let, is, or \_ as an identifier

Using `let` or `is` as the name of a class, interface, trait, enum, function, or constant (including via [define()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.define.php)) is now deprecated, as is using either as the alias in a [class_alias()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.class-alias.php) call or in a `use`, `use function`, or `use const` declaration. The names are being reserved as keywords for potential future features: `let` for block scoping and `is` for pattern matching. Rename the affected symbols.

The [deprecation of `_` as a class name in PHP 8.4](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration84.deprecated.php#migration84.deprecated.core.underscore-class-name) is extended to constants: declaring a constant named `_` with `const` or [define()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.define.php), and aliasing a class or constant to `_` in a `use` declaration, are now deprecated. Functions named `_`, including the [\_()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.-.php) alias of [gettext()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.gettext.php), are not affected.

#### Third argument to define()

Passing the `case_insensitive` argument to [define()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.define.php) is now deprecated. Case-insensitive constants were removed in PHP 8.0, since when the argument has been ignored. Explicitly passing **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)** now emits a deprecation notice. Passing **[`true`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.true)** continues to emit a warning, whose message now states that this will become an error in PHP 9.0. Omit the argument.

#### is_a() and is_subclass_of() with a string when allow_string is false

Calling [is_a()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-a.php) or [is_subclass_of()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-subclass-of.php) with a string as the first argument while `allow_string` is **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)** is now deprecated. In that case the functions always return **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)**, even when the class is already loaded, so such a call indicates a bug. To avoid triggering autoloading, check [class_exists()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.class-exists.php) with autoloading disabled first, and then call the function with `allow_string` set to **[`true`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.true)**.

#### metaphone()

The [metaphone()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.metaphone.php) function is now deprecated. It implements the original 1990 Metaphone algorithm, which is limited to English pronunciation rules and has long been superseded by Double Metaphone and Metaphone 3. Phonetic algorithms are language-specific and frequently updated, so they are better served by a userland library; use one instead.

#### More than 16 filters in a php://filter URL

Using more than 16 filters in a [php://filter](https://www.php.net/manual/en/wrappers.php.php) URL without configuring the `filter.max_filter_count` stream context option now emits a deprecation notice. Long filter chains have no known legitimate use, but are the basis of a class of attacks that turn a local file inclusion or an arbitrary file read into remote code execution. When `filter.max_filter_count` is set explicitly, exceeding it is already an error: opening the stream fails with a warning.

Code that needs more filters should either add them with [stream_filter_append()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-filter-append.php) or [stream_filter_prepend()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-filter-prepend.php), which are not limited, or raise the limit through the context option, for example globally with [stream_context_set_default()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-context-set-default.php).

#### Passing objects to array_walk(), array_walk_recursive(), and http_build_query()

Passing an object as the `array` argument to [array_walk()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.array-walk.php) or [array_walk_recursive()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.array-walk-recursive.php) is now deprecated. A small number of functions silently interpret an object as the array of its visible properties. Modifying such properties through a by-reference callback violates [readonly](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.properties.php#language.oop5.properties.readonly-properties) semantics and can corrupt enum cases, and [array_walk_recursive()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.array-walk-recursive.php) does not recurse into nested objects anyway. Call [get_object_vars()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.get-object-vars.php) on the object first and pass the resulting array.

Passing an object as the `data` argument to [http_build_query()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.http-build-query.php) is now deprecated. Objects encountered as values within `data` now also emit a deprecation notice when they are interpreted as arrays. Treating objects as arrays has been a recurring source of confusion, in particular for [Stringable](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.stringable.php) objects, which users expect to be converted to a string instead. Convert objects to arrays with [get_object_vars()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.get-object-vars.php), recursively if necessary, before calling the function.

#### is_double(), is_long(), is_integer(), and doubleval()

Following the [deprecation of the non-canonical cast names in PHP 8.5](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration85.deprecated.php#migration85.deprecated.core.non-canonical-cast-names), the function aliases that carry the same outdated type names are now deprecated. They behave identically to their canonical counterparts, which should be used instead:

- [is_double()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-double.php) =\> [is_float()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-float.php)
- [is_long()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-long.php) =\> [is_int()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-int.php)
- [is_integer()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-integer.php) =\> [is_int()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.is-int.php)
- [doubleval()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.doubleval.php) =\> [floatval()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.floatval.php)

#### strcoll() and SORT_LOCALE_STRING

The [strcoll()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.strcoll.php) function is now deprecated. It compares strings according to the `LC_COLLATE` setting of the current locale, which is global process state set via [setlocale()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.setlocale.php) that any library can change, it is not binary safe unlike every other string comparison function, and some locales do not implement correct collation rules. Use [Collator::compare()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/collator.compare.php) from the [intl](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.intl.php) extension instead, which is accurate and has up-to-date collation rules.

The **[`SORT_LOCALE_STRING`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/array.constants.php#constant.sort-locale-string)** flag of the sort functions is now deprecated for the same reasons, as it sorts using [strcoll()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.strcoll.php). Use one of the following methods of the [Collator](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.collator.php) class instead:

- [Collator::sort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/collator.sort.php)
- [Collator::asort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/collator.asort.php)
- [Collator::sortWithSortKeys()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/collator.sortwithsortkeys.php)

### Bzip2

Passing an object as the parameters of the [bzip2.compress and bzip2.decompress](https://www.php.net/manual/en/filters.compression.php) stream filters is now deprecated, as only an associative array is documented and supported. Call [get_object_vars()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.get-object-vars.php) on the object first and pass the resulting array.

### GMP

The shift (`<<`, `>>`) and exponentiation (`**`) operators on [GMP](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.gmp.php) objects now emit a deprecation notice when the right operand is a [float](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.float.php) whose conversion to [int](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.integer.php) loses precision, consistent with the deprecation of implicit lossy float to int conversions elsewhere in the language.

### MBString

The mbregex functions have been deprecated, because the underlying Oniguruma library is no longer maintained; its maintenance ended in April 2025. The functions will be removed in PHP 9.0. For most use cases the [PCRE](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.pcre.php) functions with the `u` modifier are a suitable replacement. The affected functions are:

- [mb_ereg()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg.php)
- [mb_ereg_match()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-match.php)
- [mb_ereg_replace()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-replace.php)
- [mb_ereg_replace_callback()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-replace-callback.php)
- [mb_ereg_search()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-search.php)
- [mb_ereg_search_getpos()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-search-getpos.php)
- [mb_ereg_search_getregs()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-search-getregs.php)
- [mb_ereg_search_init()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-search-init.php)
- [mb_ereg_search_pos()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-search-pos.php)
- [mb_ereg_search_regs()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-search-regs.php)
- [mb_ereg_search_setpos()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-ereg-search-setpos.php)
- [mb_eregi()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-eregi.php)
- [mb_eregi_replace()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-eregi-replace.php)
- [mb_regex_encoding()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-regex-encoding.php)
- [mb_regex_set_options()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-regex-set-options.php)
- [mb_split()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-split.php)

The **[`MB_ONIGURUMA_VERSION`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mbstring.constants.php#constant.mb-oniguruma-version)** constant and the [mbstring.regex_retry_limit](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mbstring.configuration.php#ini.mbstring.regex-retry-limit) and [mbstring.regex_stack_limit](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mbstring.configuration.php#ini.mbstring.regex-stack-limit) INI directives are deprecated along with them.

Passing an object as the `vars` argument to [mb_convert_variables()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-convert-variables.php) is now deprecated, as objects are silently interpreted as the array of their visible properties. Call [get_object_vars()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.get-object-vars.php) on the object first, or use [mb_convert_encoding()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mb-convert-encoding.php), which converts arrays recursively and returns the result instead of modifying its argument in place.

### MySQLi

The [mysqli_get_charset()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.get-charset.php) function and the [mysqli::get_charset()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.get-charset.php) method are now deprecated, without replacement. They expose internal implementation details of the character set that have been meaningless since the switch to mysqlnd; in particular the reported collation does not correspond to the collation defined by the server. To get the name of the current character set, use [mysqli_character_set_name()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.character-set-name.php) or [mysqli::character_set_name()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.character-set-name.php).

The [mysqli_stmt_init()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.stmt-init.php) function and the [mysqli::stmt_init()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.stmt-init.php) method are now deprecated. They create an empty statement object that still has to be prepared before use, and are a source of statement objects left in an inconsistent state. Use [mysqli_prepare()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.prepare.php) or [mysqli::prepare()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli.prepare.php) instead, which prepare the statement in one step. For the same reason, calling the [mysqli_stmt::\_\_construct()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli-stmt.construct.php) constructor without the `query` parameter is now deprecated; pass the query to the constructor instead.

### Reflection

Calling [ReflectionProperty::setValue()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reflectionproperty.setvalue.php) or [ReflectionProperty::setRawValue()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reflectionproperty.setrawvalue.php) with an object that is not an instance of the class on which the property was declared is now deprecated. Unlike the other [ReflectionProperty](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.reflectionproperty.php) methods, which throw for such objects, these methods silently set a property on the unrelated object, which is no better than a normal assignment and conceptually wrong.

Passing an object to [ReflectionMethod::invoke()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reflectionmethod.invoke.php) or [ReflectionMethod::invokeArgs()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reflectionmethod.invokeargs.php) when invoking a static method is now deprecated. Static methods have no `$this`, so the object was ignored entirely and never validated. Pass **[`null`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.null)** instead.

### Session

Passing an object that does not implement both the [SessionIdInterface::create_sid()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/sessionidinterface.create-sid.php) and [SessionUpdateTimestampHandlerInterface::validateId()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/sessionupdatetimestamphandlerinterface.validateid.php) methods to [session_set_save_handler()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.session-set-save-handler.php) is now deprecated, regardless of which interfaces the object declares. These methods are required for a save handler to behave correctly under [session.use_strict_mode](https://www.php.net/manual/en/session.configuration.php#ini.session.use-strict-mode), which is [enabled by default as of PHP 8.6](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration86.incompatible.php#migration86.incompatible.session) and mitigates session fixation.

Accordingly, an **[`E_WARNING`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/errorfunc.constants.php#constant.e-warning)** is now emitted when a class implements [SessionHandlerInterface](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.sessionhandlerinterface.php) without defining the [SessionIdInterface::create_sid()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/sessionidinterface.create-sid.php) or [SessionUpdateTimestampHandlerInterface::validateId()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/sessionupdatetimestamphandlerinterface.validateid.php) methods. In PHP 9.0 these methods will be moved from [SessionIdInterface](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.sessionidinterface.php) and [SessionUpdateTimestampHandlerInterface](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.sessionupdatetimestamphandlerinterface.php) into [SessionHandlerInterface](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.sessionhandlerinterface.php), where they will be required. Implement both methods on custom save handlers now.

### SPL

The [spl_classes()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-classes.php) function is now deprecated. No other extension exposes such a function, and the Reflection extension is always available. Use [ReflectionExtension::getClassNames()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reflectionextension.getclassnames.php) instead.

The [spl_object_hash()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-object-hash.php) function is now deprecated. Since PHP 8.1 its return value has been nothing more than a reformatted [spl_object_id()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-object-id.php), and the name is misleading as the value is not derived from the contents of the object. The string form is also error-prone: two hashes can compare loosely equal because both are numeric strings. Use [spl_object_id()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-object-id.php) instead.

The following [ArrayIterator](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.arrayiterator.php) methods are now deprecated. They only exist because [ArrayIterator](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.arrayiterator.php) historically shared its implementation with [ArrayObject](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.arrayobject.php); most of them make little sense on an iterator and prevent optimizing its implementation. The corresponding [ArrayObject](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.arrayobject.php) methods are not deprecated.

- [ArrayIterator::getFlags()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.getflags.php)
- [ArrayIterator::setFlags()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.setflags.php)
- [ArrayIterator::asort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.asort.php)
- [ArrayIterator::ksort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.ksort.php)
- [ArrayIterator::uasort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.uasort.php)
- [ArrayIterator::uksort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.uksort.php)
- [ArrayIterator::natsort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.natsort.php)
- [ArrayIterator::natcasesort()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.natcasesort.php)
- [ArrayIterator::unserialize()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.unserialize.php)
- [ArrayIterator::serialize()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/arrayiterator.serialize.php)

The CSV methods of [SplFileObject](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.splfileobject.php) are now deprecated. Their historical design inconsistencies, further exposed by named arguments, have made them increasingly difficult to maintain, and CSV handling does not naturally belong in [SplFileObject](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.splfileobject.php). Use [fgetcsv()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.fgetcsv.php) and [fputcsv()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.fputcsv.php) on a stream instead.

- [SplFileObject::fgetcsv()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splfileobject.fgetcsv.php)
- [SplFileObject::fputcsv()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splfileobject.fputcsv.php)
- [SplFileObject::setCsvControl()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splfileobject.setcsvcontrol.php)
- [SplFileObject::getCsvControl()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splfileobject.getcsvcontrol.php)

### Zlib

Passing an object as the parameters of the [zlib.deflate and zlib.inflate](https://www.php.net/manual/en/filters.compression.php) stream filters is now deprecated, as only an associative array is documented and supported. Call [get_object_vars()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.get-object-vars.php) on the object first and pass the resulting array.

Passing an object as the `options` argument to [deflate_init()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.deflate-init.php) or [inflate_init()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.inflate-init.php) is now deprecated, as objects are silently interpreted as the array of their visible properties. Call [get_object_vars()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.get-object-vars.php) on the object first and pass the resulting array.

# [PHP 8.5](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration85.deprecated.php)

## Deprecated Features

### PHP Core

#### Changes to user output handler

Trying to produce output (e.g. with [echo](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.echo.php)) within a user output handler is deprecated. The deprecation warning will bypass the handler producing the output to ensure it is visible; if there are nested output handlers the next one will still be used.

#### Non-canonical cast names

Non-canonical cast names `(boolean)`, `(integer)`, `(double)`, and `(binary)` have been deprecated, use `(bool)`, `(int)`, `(float)`, and `(string)` respectively.

#### Terminating case statements with a semicolon

Terminating case statements with a semicolon instead of a colon has been deprecated.

#### The backtick operator

[The backtick operator](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.operators.execution.php) as an alias for [shell_exec()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.shell-exec.php) has been deprecated.

#### Returning null from \_\_debugInfo()

Returning **[`null`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.null)** from [\_\_debugInfo()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.magic.php#language.oop5.magic.debuginfo) has been deprecated. Return an empty array instead.

#### report_memleaks INI directive

The [report_memleaks](https://www.php.net/manual/en/errorfunc.configuration.php#ini.report-memleaks) INI directive has been deprecated.

#### Constant redeclaration

Constant redeclaration has been deprecated. Note that this already generated a warning and will continue to do so.

#### Closure binding issues

The following closure binding issues, which already emit an **[`E_WARNING`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/errorfunc.constants.php#constant.e-warning)**, are now deprecated:

- Binding an instance to a static closure.
- Binding methods to objects that are not instances of the class (or subclass) that the method is defined.
- Unbinding \$this from a method.
- Unbinding \$this from a closure that uses \`\$this\`.
- Binding a closure to the scope of an internal class.
- Rebinding the scope of a closure created from a function or method.

#### \_\_sleep() and \_\_wakeup() magic methods

The [\_\_sleep()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.magic.php#object.sleep) and [\_\_wakeup()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.magic.php#object.wakeup) magic methods have been soft-deprecated. The [\_\_serialize()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.magic.php#object.serialize) and [\_\_unserialize()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.magic.php#object.unserialize) magic methods should be used instead, or at the same time if compatibility with PHP 7 is required.

#### Using null as an array offset

Using **[`null`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.null)** as an array offset or when calling [array_key_exists()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.array-key-exists.php) is now deprecated. Instead an empty string should be used.

#### Incrementing non-numeric strings

Incrementing non-numeric strings is now deprecated. Instead the [str_increment()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.str-increment.php) function should be used.

#### register_argc_argv INI directive

Deriving `$_SERVER['argc']` and `$_SERVER['argv']` from the query string for non-CLI SAPIs has been deprecated. Configure `register_argc_argv=0` and switch to either [`$_GET`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.variables.get.php) or `$_SERVER['QUERY_STRING']` to access the information, after verifying that the usage is safe.

### cURL

The [curl_close()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.curl-close.php) function has been deprecated, as [CurlHandle](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.curlhandle.php) objects are freed automatically.

The [curl_share_close()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.curl-share-close.php) function has been deprecated, as [CurlShareHandle](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.curlsharehandle.php) objects are freed automatically.

### Date

The **[`DATE_RFC7231`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/datetime.constants.php#constant.date-rfc7231)** and **[`DateTimeInterface::RFC7231`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.datetimeinterface.php#datetimeinterface.constants.rfc7231)** constants have been deprecated. This is because the associated timezone is ignored and always uses GMT.

### FileInfo

The [finfo_close()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.finfo-close.php) function has been deprecated. As [finfo](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.finfo.php) objects are freed automatically.

The `context` parameter of the [finfo_buffer()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.finfo-buffer.php) function has been deprecated as it is ignored.

### GD

The [imagedestroy()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.imagedestroy.php) function has been deprecated, as [GdImage](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.gdimage.php) objects are freed automatically.

### Hash

The **[`MHASH_*`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mhash.constants.php#constant.mhash-adler32)** constants have been deprecated.

### Intl

The [intl.error_level](https://www.php.net/manual/en/intl.configuration.php#ini.intl.error-level) INI setting has been deprecated. Errors should either be checked manually or exceptions should be enabled by using the [intl.use_exceptions](https://www.php.net/manual/en/intl.configuration.php#ini.intl.use-exceptions) INI setting.

### LDAP

Specific Oracle Instant Client calls and constants have been deprecated. List of affected calls:

- [ldap_connect()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.ldap-connect.php) with wallet support
- [ldap_connect_wallet()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.ldap-connect-wallet.php)

List of affected constants:

- **`GSLC_SSL_NO_UATH`**
- **`GSLC_SSL_ONEWAY_UATH`**
- **`GSLC_SSL_TWOWAY_UATH`**

### MySQLi

The [mysqli_execute()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.mysqli-execute.php) alias function has been deprecated. Use [mysqli_stmt_execute()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/mysqli-stmt.execute.php) instead.

### OpenSSL

The `key_length` parameter for [openssl_pkey_derive()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-pkey-derive.php) has been deprecated. This is because it is either ignored, or truncates the key, which can be a security vulnerability.

### PDO

The `"uri:"` DSN scheme has been deprecated due to security concerns with DSNs coming from remote URIs.

Driver specific constants in the PDO class have been deprecated. List of affected constants and their replacement:

- **`PDO::DBLIB_ATTR_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT`** =\> **[`Pdo\Dblib::ATTR_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-dblib.php#pdo-dblib.constants.attr-connection-timeout)**
- **`PDO::DBLIB_ATTR_QUERY_TIMEOUT`** =\> **[`Pdo\Dblib::ATTR_QUERY_TIMEOUT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-dblib.php#pdo-dblib.constants.attr-query-timeout)**
- **`PDO::DBLIB_ATTR_STRINGIFY_UNIQUEIDENTIFIER`** =\> **[`Pdo\Dblib::ATTR_STRINGIFY_UNIQUEIDENTIFIER`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-dblib.php#pdo-dblib.constants.attr-stringify-uniqueidentifier)**
- **`PDO::DBLIB_ATTR_VERSION`** =\> **[`Pdo\Dblib::ATTR_VERSION`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-dblib.php#pdo-dblib.constants.attr-version)**
- **`PDO::DBLIB_ATTR_TDS_VERSION`** =\> **[`Pdo\Dblib::ATTR_TDS_VERSION`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-dblib.php#pdo-dblib.constants.attr-tds-version)**
- **`PDO::DBLIB_ATTR_SKIP_EMPTY_ROWSETS`** =\> **[`Pdo\Dblib::ATTR_SKIP_EMPTY_ROWSETS`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-dblib.php#pdo-dblib.constants.attr-skip-empty-rowsets)**
- **`PDO::DBLIB_ATTR_DATETIME_CONVERT`** =\> **[`Pdo\Dblib::ATTR_DATETIME_CONVERT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-dblib.php#pdo-dblib.constants.attr-datetime-convert)**
- **[`PDO::FB_ATTR_DATE_FORMAT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-firebird.php#pdo.constants.fb-attr-date-format)** =\> **[`Pdo\Firebird::ATTR_DATE_FORMAT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-firebird.php#pdo-firebird.constants.attr-date-format)**
- **[`PDO::FB_ATTR_TIME_FORMAT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-firebird.php#pdo.constants.fb-attr-time-format)** =\> **[`Pdo\Firebird::ATTR_TIME_FORMAT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-firebird.php#pdo-firebird.constants.attr-time-format)**
- **[`PDO::FB_ATTR_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-firebird.php#pdo.constants.fb-attr-timestamp-format)** =\> **[`Pdo\Firebird::ATTR_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-firebird.php#pdo-firebird.constants.attr-timestamp-format)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-use-buffered-query)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-use-buffered-query)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_LOCAL_INFILE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-local-infile)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_LOCAL_INFILE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-local-infile)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_LOCAL_INFILE_DIRECTORY`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-local-infile-directory)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_LOCAL_INFILE_DIRECTORY`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-local-infile-directory)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_INIT_COMMAND`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-init-command)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_INIT_COMMAND`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-init-command)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-max-buffer-size)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-max-buffer-size)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_READ_DEFAULT_FILE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-read-default-file)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_READ_DEFAULT_FILE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-read-default-file)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_READ_DEFAULT_GROUP`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-read-default-group)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_READ_DEFAULT_GROUP`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-read-default-group)**
- **[`PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_COMPRESS`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-compress)** =\> **[`Pdo\Mysql::ATTR_COMPRESS`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.pdo-mysql.php#pdo-mysql.constants.attr-compress)**

- [PDO::sqliteCreateAggregate()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo.sqlitecreateaggregate.php) =\> [Pdo\Sqlite::createAggregate()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo-sqlite.createaggregate.php)

- [PDO::sqliteCreateFunction()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo.sqlitecreatefunction.php) =\> [Pdo\Sqlite::createFunction()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo-sqlite.createfunction.php)

### PDO_PGSQL

Constants related to transaction states have been deprecated as this feature is unavailable with PDO:

- **[`PDO::PGSQL_TRANSACTION_IDLE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-pgsql.php#pdo.constants.pgsql-transaction-idle)**
- **[`PDO::PGSQL_TRANSACTION_ACTIVE`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-pgsql.php#pdo.constants.pgsql-transaction-active)**
- **[`PDO::PGSQL_TRANSACTION_INTRANS`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-pgsql.php#pdo.constants.pgsql-transaction-intrans)**
- **[`PDO::PGSQL_TRANSACTION_INERROR`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-pgsql.php#pdo.constants.pgsql-transaction-inerror)**
- **[`PDO::PGSQL_TRANSACTION_UNKNOWN`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-pgsql.php#pdo.constants.pgsql-transaction-unknown)**

### Reflection

The `setAccessible()` methods of various Reflection objects have been deprecated, as those no longer have an effect.

Calling [ReflectionClass::getConstant()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reflectionclass.getconstant.php) for constants that do not exist has been deprecated.

Calling [ReflectionProperty::getDefaultValue()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reflectionproperty.getdefaultvalue.php) for properties without default values has been deprecated.

### SPL

Unregistering all autoloaders by passing the [spl_autoload_call()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-autoload-call.php) function as a callback argument to [spl_autoload_unregister()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-autoload-unregister.php) has been deprecated. Instead if this is needed, one should iterate over the return value of [spl_autoload_functions()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-autoload-functions.php) and call [spl_autoload_unregister()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.spl-autoload-unregister.php) on each value.

The [SplObjectStorage::contains()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.contains.php), [SplObjectStorage::attach()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.attach.php), and [SplObjectStorage::detach()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.detach.php) methods have been deprecated in favour of [SplObjectStorage::offsetExists()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.offsetexists.php), [SplObjectStorage::offsetSet()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.offsetset.php), and [SplObjectStorage::offsetUnset()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.offsetunset.php) respectively.

Using [ArrayObject](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.arrayobject.php) and [ArrayIterator](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.arrayiterator.php) with objects has been deprecated.

### Standard

The [socket_set_timeout()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.socket-set-timeout.php) alias function has been deprecated. Use [stream_set_timeout()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-set-timeout.php) instead.

Passing **[`null`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.null)** to [readdir()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.readdir.php), [rewinddir()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.rewinddir.php), and [closedir()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.closedir.php) to use the last opened directory has been deprecated. Provide the last opened directory explicitly instead.

Passing integers outside the interval `[0, 255]` to [chr()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.chr.php) is now deprecated. This is because a byte can only hold a value within this interval.

Passing a string which is not a single byte to [ord()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.ord.php) is now deprecated, this is indicative of a bug.

The locally predefined variable [\$http_response_header](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.variables.httpresponseheader.php) is deprecated. Instead one should call the [http_get_last_response_headers()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.http-get-last-response-headers.php) function.

### XML

The [xml_parser_free()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.xml-parser-free.php) function has been deprecated, as [XMLParser](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.xmlparser.php) objects are freed automatically.

# [PHP 8.4](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration84.deprecated.php)
