# [Other changes to extensions in PHP 5.5, 5.4, 5.3](index.md)

# [PHP 5.5](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration55.extensions-other.php)

## Other changes to extensions

### [Intl](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.intl.html)

The [intl](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.intl.html) extension now requires ICU 4.0 or later.

# [PHP 5.4](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration54.extensions-other.php)

## Other changes to extensions

Changes in extension behavior, and new features:

- [mysqli](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysqli.html) - [mysqli_result](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.mysqli-result.html) now implements [Traversable](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.traversable.html)

&nbsp;

- [pdo_mysql](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.pdo-mysql.html) - Removed support for linking with MySQL client libraries older than 4.1

&nbsp;

- The MySQL extensions [mysql](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysql.html), [mysqli](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysqli.html) and [PDO_mysql](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.pdo-mysql.html) use [mysqlnd](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysqlnd.html) as the default library now. It is still possible to use libmysqlclient by specifying a path to the configure options.

&nbsp;

- [mysqlnd](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysqlnd.html) - Added named pipes support

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.extensions-other.php)

## Other changes to extensions

The following extensions can no longer be disabled during build configuration:

- [PCRE](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.pcre.html)
- [Reflection](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.reflection.html)
- [SPL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.spl.html)

Changes in extension behaviour, and new features:

- [Date and Time](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.datetime.html) - The TZ environment variable is no longer used to guess the timezone
- [cURL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.curl.html) - cURL now supports SSH
- [Network](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.network.html) - [dns_check_record()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.dns-check-record.html) now returns an extra "entries" index, containing the TXT elements.
- [Hash](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.hash.html) - The SHA-224 and salsa hash algorithms are now supported.
- [mbstring](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mbstring.html) - Now supports CP850 encoding.
- [OCI8](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.oci8.html) - A call to [oci_close()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.oci-close.html) on a persistent connection, or a variable referencing a persistent connection going out of scope, will now roll back any uncommitted transaction. To avoid unexpected behavior, explicitly issue a commit or roll back as needed. The old behavior can be enabled with the INI directive [oci8.old_oci_close_semantics](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/oci8.configuration.html#ini.oci8.old-oci-close-semantics). Database Resident Connection Pooling (DRCP) and Fast Application Notification (FAN) are now supported. Oracle External Authentication is now supported (except on Windows). The [oci_bind_by_name()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.oci-bind-by-name.html) function now supports SQLT_AFC (aka the CHAR datatype).
- [OpenSSL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.openssl.html) - OpenSSL digest and cipher functions are now supported. It is also now possible to access the internal values of DSA, RSA and DH keys.
- [Session](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.session.html) - Sessions will no longer store session-files in `"/tmp"` when [open_basedir](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.open-basedir) restrictions apply, unless `"/tmp"` is explicitly added to the list of allowed paths.
- [SOAP](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.soap.html) Now supports sending user supplied HTTP headers.
- [MySQLi](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysqli.html) Now supports persistent connections, by prepending the hostname with `"p:"`.
- [Image Processing and GD](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.image.html) The "JPG Support" index returned from [gd_info()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.gd-info.html) has been renamed to "JPEG Support".

# [Other changes in PHP 5.4, 5.3, 5.2](index.md)

# [PHP 5.4](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration54.other.php)

## Other changes

- **`E_ALL`** now includes **`E_STRICT`** level errors in the [error_reporting](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/errorfunc.configuration.html#ini.error-reporting) configuration directive.
- [SNMP](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.snmp.html) now has an OOP API. Functions now return **`FALSE`** on every error condition including SNMP-related (no such instance, end of MIB, etc). Thus, in particular, breaks previous behavior of get/walk functions returning an empty string on SNMP-related errors. Multi OID get/getnext/set queries are now supported. Dropped UCD-SNMP compatibility code, consider upgrading to net-snmp v5.3+, Net-SNMP v5.4+ is required for Windows version. In sake of adding support for IPv6 DNS name resolution of remote SNMP agent (peer) is done by extension now, not by Net-SNMP library anymore.
- [OpenSSL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.openssl.html) now supports AES.
- [CLI SAPI](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/features.commandline.html) doesn't terminate any more on fatal errors when using interactive mode with readline support.
- [\$\_SERVER\['REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT'\]](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.variables.superglobals.html) has been added to include microsecond precision.
- Added new hash algorithms: fnv132, fnv164, joaat
- Chained string offsets - e.g. \$a\[0\]\[0\] where \$a is a string - now work.
- Arrays cast from [SimpleXMLElement](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.simplexmlelement.html) now *always* contain all nodes instead of just the first matching node. All [SimpleXMLElement](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.simplexmlelement.html) children are now *always* printed when using [var_dump()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.var-dump.html), [var_export()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.var-export.html) and [print_r()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.print-r.html).
- It's now possible to enforce the class' [\_\_construct](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.decon.html) arguments in an abstract constructor in the base class.

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.other.php)

## Other changes

- [SplFileInfo::getpathinfo()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/splfileinfo.getpathinfo.html) now returns information about the path name.
- [SplObjectStorage](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.splobjectstorage.html) now has [ArrayAccess](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.arrayaccess.html) support. It is now also possible to store associative information with objects in [SplObjectStorage](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/class.splobjectstorage.html).
- In the GD extension, there is now pixelation support available through the [imagefilter()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.imagefilter.html) function.
- [var_dump()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.var-dump.html) output now includes private object properties.
- [session_start()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.session-start.html) now returns **`FALSE`** when session startup fails.
- [property_exists()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.property-exists.html) now checks the existence of a property independent of accessibility (like [method_exists()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.method-exists.html)).
- [Stream wrappers](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/wrappers.html) can now be used by [include_path](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.include-path).
- The `initial` parameter for [array_reduce()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.array-reduce.html) can now be of any type.
- The [directory functions](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.dir.html) [opendir()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.opendir.html), [scandir()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.scandir.html), and [dir()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.dir.html) now use the default stream context if no explicit context is passed.
- [crypt()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.crypt.html) now has Blowfish and extended DES support, and [crypt()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.crypt.html) features are now 100% portable. PHP has its own internal crypt implementation which drops into place when support for `crypt` or `crypt_r` is not found.
- [getopt()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.getopt.html) now accepts "long options" on all platforms. Optional values and `=` as a separator for short options are now supported.
- [fopen()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.fopen.html) has a new mode option (`n`), which passes **`O_NONBLOCK`** to the underlying `open()` system call. Note that this mode is not currently supported on Windows.
- [getimagesize()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.getimagesize.html) now supports icon files (.ico).
- The mhash extension have moved to PECL, but the [Hash](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.hash.html) extension have been modified to support mhash if PHP is compiled with `--with-mhash`. Note that the Hash extension does not require the mhash library to be available whether or not the mhash emulation is enabled.

# [PHP 5.2](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration52.other.php)

## Other Enhancements

- Improved memory manager and increased default memory limit. The new memory manager allocates less memory and works faster than the previous incarnation. It allocates memory from the system in large blocks, and then manages the heap by itself. The `memory_limit` value in `php.ini` is checked, not for each `emalloc()` call (as before), but for actual blocks requested from the system. This means that `memory_limit` is far more accurate than it used to be, since the old memory manager didn't calculate all the memory overhead used by the `malloc` library. Thanks to this new-found accuracy memory usage may appear to have increased, although actually it has not. To accommodate this apparent increase, the default `memory_limit` setting was also increased - from 8 to 16 megabytes.
- Added support for constructors in interfaces to force constructor signature checks in implementations. Starting with PHP 5.2.0, interfaces can have constructors. However, if you choose to declare a constructor in an interface, each class implementing that interface MUST include a constructor with a signature matching that of the base interface constructor. By 'signature' we mean the parameter and return type definitions, including any type hints and including whether the data is passed by reference or by value.

Intl:

# [PHP 5.5](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration55.ini.php)

## Changes to INI file handling

### [Intl](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.intl.html)

The `intl.use_exceptions` configuration directive has been added, which controls the behaviour of intl when global errors occur in conjunction with the already extant `intl.error_level` configuration directive.

### [MySQLnd](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysqlnd.html)

The [mysqlnd.sha256_server_public_key](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/mysqlnd.config.html#ini.mysqlnd.sha256-server-public-key) configuration directive has been added to allow [mysqli](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.mysqli.html) to use the new MySQL authentication protocol.

# [PHP 5.4](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration54.ini.php)

The following `php.ini` directives have been removed:

- mbstring.script_encoding
- [y2k_compliance](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.y2k-compliance)

The following `php.ini` directives have been added:

- [cli.pager](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/readline.configuration.html#ini.cli.pager) and [cli.prompt](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/readline.configuration.html#ini.cli.prompt) for CLI SAPI using readline in interactive mode.
- [cli_server.color](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/features.commandline.ini.html#ini.cli-server.color) to enable the built-in development web server to use ANSI color coding in terminal output.
- [max_input_vars](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/info.configuration.html#ini.max-input-vars) - specifies how many GET/POST/COOKIE input variables may be accepted.
- [zend.multibyte](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend.multibyte) - to control the new multibyte support.
- [zend.script_encoding](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend.script-encoding) - This value will be used unless a "declare(encoding=...)" directive appears at the top of the script.
- [zend.signal_check](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend.signal-check) - to check for replaced signal handlers on shutdown.
- [session.upload_progress.enabled](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.upload-progress.enabled), [session.upload_progress.cleanup](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.upload-progress.cleanup), [session.upload_progress.prefix](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.upload-progress.prefix), [session.upload_progress.name](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.upload-progress.name), [session.upload_progress.freq](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.upload-progress.freq), [session.upload_progress.min_freq](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.upload-progress.min-freq)
- [enable_post_data_reading](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.enable-post-data-reading) - When it's disabled, the POST data is not read (and processed)
- [windows_show_crt_warning](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.windows-show-crt-warning) - This directive shows the Windows CRT warnings when enabled. These warnings were displayed by default until now.

The following `php.ini` directives have been changed:

- [session.entropy_file](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.entropy-file) now defaults to /dev/random or /dev/urandom depending on what has been guessed at compile time.
- [session.entropy_length](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.entropy-length) now defaults to 32.

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.ini.php)

## Changes to INI file handling

PHP 5.3.0 has significantly improved performance and parsing of INI files, and adds several new syntax features.

- The standard `php.ini` files have been re-organized and renamed. `php.ini-development` contains settings recommended for use in development environments. `php.ini-production` contains settings recommended for use in production environments.
- There is now support for two special sections: `[PATH=/opt/httpd/www.example.com/]` and `[HOST=www.example.com]`. Directives set in these sections cannot be overridden by user-defined INI files or at runtime. More information about these sections can be found [here](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.sections.html).
- [zend_extension_debug](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend-extension-debug), [zend_extension_debug_ts](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend-extension-debug-ts) and [zend_extension_ts](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend-extension-ts) have been removed. Use the [zend_extension](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend-extension) directive to load all Zend Extensions.
- [zend.ze1_compatibility_mode](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend.ze1-compatibility-mode) has been removed. If this INI directive is set to On, an **`E_ERROR`** error is emitted at startup.
- It is now possible to use the full path to load modules using the [extension](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.extension) directive.
- `"ini-variables"` can now be used almost anywhere in a `php.ini` file.
- [open_basedir](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.open-basedir) restrictions may now be tighted at runtime, and the directive is now PHP_INI_ALL.
- It is now possible to use alphanumeric or variable indices in INI option arrays.
- [get_cfg_var()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.get-cfg-var.html) is now able to return "array" INI options.
- Two new mail directives: [mail.add_x_header](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/mail.configuration.html#ini.mail.add-x-header) and [mail.log](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/mail.configuration.html#ini.mail.log), have been added.

The following new ini directives have been added:

- `user_ini.filename` and `user_ini.cache_ttl` have been added to control the use of [user INI files](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/configuration.file.per-user.html).
- [exit_on_timeout](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.exit-on-timeout) has been added to force Apache 1.x children to exit if a PHP execution timeout occurs.
- Added `mbstring.http_output_conv_mimetype`. This directive specifies the regex pattern of content types for which [mb_output_handler()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mb-output-handler.html) is activated.
- Added [request_order](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.request-order). Allows controlling which external variables will be available in [`$_REQUEST`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.request.html).

The following ini directives have new default values:

- [session.use_only_cookies](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.use-only-cookies) is now set to `"1"` (enabled) by default.
- [oci8.default_prefetch](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/oci8.configuration.html#ini.oci8.default-prefetch) has changed from `"10"` to `"100"`.

# [Changes in PHP 5.2, 5.1](index.md)

# [PHP 5.2](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration52.datetime.php)

## Changes in PHP [datetime](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.datetime.html) support

Since PHP 5.1.0, there has been an extension named `date` in the PHP core. This is the new implementation of PHP's datetime support. Although it will attempt to guess your system's timezone setting, you should set the timezone manually. You can do this in any of three ways:

- in your `php.ini` using the [date.timezone](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/datetime.configuration.html#ini.date.timezone) INI directive
- on your system using the `TZ` environmental variable
- from your script using the convenience function [date_default_timezone_set()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-default-timezone-set.html)

All supported [timezones](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/timezones.html) are listed in the PHP Manual.

With the advent of PHP 5.2.x, there are [object](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.types.object.html) representations of the date and timezone, named `DateTime` and `DateTimeZone` respectively. The methods map to existing procedural date functions.

# [PHP 5.1](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.datetime.php)

## Date/time support

Date/time support has been fully rewritten in PHP 5.1.x, and no longer uses the system settings to 'know' the timezone in operation. It will instead utilize, in the following order:

- The timezone set using the [date_default_timezone_set()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.date-default-timezone-set.html) function (if any)

- The TZ environment variable (if non empty)

- "magical" guess (if the operating system supports it)

- If none of the above options succeeds, UTC

To ensure accuracy (and avoid an **`E_STRICT`** warning), you will need to define your timezone in your `php.ini` using the following format:

date.timezone = Europe/London

The supported timezones are listed, in this format, in the [timezones appendix](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/timezones.html).

Also note that [strtotime()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.strtotime.html) now returns **`FALSE`** on failure, instead of -1.

# [New INI Configuration Directives in PHP 5.2, 5.0](index.md)

# [PHP 5.2](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration52.newconf.php)

## New INI Configuration Directives

New `php.ini` directives introduced in PHP 5.2.0:

- [allow_url_include](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/filesystem.configuration.html#ini.allow-url-include) This useful option makes it possible to differentiate between standard file operations on remote files, and the inclusion of remote files. While the former is usually desirable, the latter can be a security risk if used naively. Starting with PHP 5.2.0, you can allow remote file operations while disallowing the inclusion of remote files in local scripts. In fact, this is the default configuration.
- [pcre.backtrack_limit](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/pcre.configuration.html#ini.pcre.backtrack-limit) PCRE's backtracking limit.
- [pcre.recursion_limit](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/pcre.configuration.html#ini.pcre.recursion-limit) PCRE's recursion limit. Please note that if you set this value to a high number you may consume all the available process stack and eventually crash PHP (due to reaching the stack size limit imposed by the Operating System).
- [session.cookie_httponly](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.cookie-httponly) Marks the cookie as accessible only through the HTTP protocol. This means that the cookie won't be accessible by scripting languages, such as JavaScript. This setting can effectively help to reduce identity theft through XSS attacks (although it is not supported by all browsers).

New directives in PHP 5.2.2:

- [max_input_nesting_level](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/info.configuration.html#ini.max-input-nesting-level) Limits how deep [input variables](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.variables.external.html) can be nested, default is 64.

# [PHP 5.0](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.newconf.php)

## New Directives

There were some new `php.ini` directives introduced in PHP 5. Here is a list of them:

- [mail.force_extra_parameters](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/mail.configuration.html#ini.mail.force_extra_parameters) - Force the addition of the specified parameters to be passed as extra parameters to the sendmail binary. These parameters will always replace the value of the 5th parameter to [mail()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mail.html), even in safe mode
- [register_long_arrays](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.register-long-arrays) - allow/disallow PHP to register the deprecated long `$HTTP_*_VARS`
- [session.hash_function](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.hash-function) - select a hash function (MD5 or SHA-1)
- [session.hash_bits_per_character](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/session.configuration.html#ini.session.hash-bits-per-character) - define how many bits are stored in each character when converting the binary hash data to something readable (from 4 to 6)
- [zend.ze1_compatibility_mode](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend.ze1-compatibility-mode) - Enable compatibility mode with Zend Engine 1 (PHP 4)

# [Changes in database support in PHP 5.1, 5.0](index.md)

# [PHP 5.1](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.databases.php)

## Changes in database support

- [PDO overview](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.databases.html#migration51.databases-pdo)

- [Changes in MySQL support](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.databases.html#migration51.databases-mysql)

- [Changes in SQLite support](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.databases.html#migration51.databases-sqlite)

## PDO overview

[PHP Data Objects (PDO)](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/intro.pdo.html) were introduced as a PECL extension under PHP 5.0, and became part of the core PHP distribution in PHP 5.1.x. The PDO extension provides a consistent interface for database access, and is used alongside database-specific PDO drivers. Each driver may also have database-specific functions of its own, but basic data access functionality such as issuing queries and fetching data is covered by PDO functions, using the driver named in [PDO::\_\_construct()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/pdo.construct.html).

Note that the PDO extension, and its drivers, are intended to be built as shared extensions. This will enable straightforward driver upgrades from PECL, without forcing you to rebuild all of PHP.

At the point of the PHP 5.1.x release, PDO is more than ready for widespread testing and could be adopted in most situations. However, it is important to understand that PDO and its drivers are comparatively young and may be missing certain database-specific features; evaluate PDO carefully before you use it in new projects.

Legacy code will generally rely on the pre-existing database extensions, which are still maintained.

## Changes in MySQL support

In PHP 4, MySQL 3 support was built-in. With the release of PHP 5.0 there were two MySQL extensions, named 'mysql' and 'mysqli', which were designed to support MySQL \< 4.1 and MySQL 4.1 and up, respectively. With the introduction of PDO, which provides a very fast interface to all the database APIs supported by PHP, the PDO_MYSQL driver can support any of the current versions (MySQL 3, 4 or 5) in PHP code written for PDO, depending on the MySQL library version used during compilation. The older MySQL extensions remain in place for reasons of back compatibility, but are not enabled by default.

## Changes in SQLite support

In PHP 5.0.x, SQLite 2 support was provided by the built-in sqlite extension, which was also available as a PECL extension in PHP 4.3 and PHP 4.4. With the introduction of PDO, the sqlite extension doubles up to act as a 'sqlite2' driver for PDO; it is due to this that the sqlite extension in PHP 5.1.x has a dependency upon the PDO extension.

PHP 5.1.x ships with a number of alternative interfaces to sqlite:

The sqlite extension provides the "classic" sqlite procedural/OO API that you may have used in prior versions of PHP. It also provides the PDO 'sqlite2' driver, which allows you to access legacy SQLite 2 databases using the PDO API.

PDO_SQLITE provides the 'sqlite' version 3 driver. SQLite version 3 is vastly superior to SQLite version 2, but the file formats of the two versions are not compatible.

If your SQLite-based project is already written and working against earlier PHP versions, then you can continue to use ext/sqlite without problems, but will need to explicitly enable both PDO and sqlite. New projects should use PDO and the 'sqlite' (version 3) driver, as this is faster than SQLite 2, has improved locking concurrency, and supports both prepared statements and binary columns natively.

You must enable PDO to use the SQLite extension. If you want to build the PDO extension as a shared extension, then the SQLite extension must also be built shared. The same holds true for any extension that provides a PDO driver

# [PHP 5.0](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.databases.php)

## Databases

There were some changes in PHP 5 regarding databases (MySQL and SQLite).

In PHP 5 the MySQL client libraries are not bundled, because of license and maintenance problems. MySQL is supported with the only change being that MySQL support is no longer enabled by *default* in PHP 5. This essentially means that PHP doesn't include the **--with-mysql** option in the [configure](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/configuration.html) line so that you must now manually do this when compiling PHP. Windows users will need to edit `php.ini` and enable the `php_mysql.dll` DLL as in PHP 4 no such DLL existed, it was simply built into your Windows PHP binaries.

There is also a new extension, [MySQLi (Improved MySQL)](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.mysqli.html), which is designed to work with MySQL 4.1 and above.

Since PHP 5, the [SQLite](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.sqlite.html) extension is built-in PHP. SQLite is an embeddable SQL database engine and is not a client library used to connect to a big database server (like MySQL or PostgreSQL). The SQLite library reads and writes directly to and from the database files on disk.

# [Changes in SAPI modules in PHP 5.4, 5.3](index.md)

# [PHP 5.4](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration54.sapi.php)

## Changes in SAPI modules

- A new SAPI module named `cli-server` is now available.
- Added CLI option `--rz` which shows information of the named Zend extension.
- Added shortcut `#inisetting=value` to change `php.ini` settings at run-time in interactive readline CLI
- Added apache compatible functions: [apache_child_terminate()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.apache-child-terminate.html), [getallheaders()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.getallheaders.html), [apache_request_headers()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.apache-request-headers.html) and [apache_response_headers()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.apache-response-headers.html) for FastCGI SAPI.
- PHP-FPM: Added the `process.max` setting, to control the number of processes that FPM can fork.

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.sapi.php)

## Changes in SAPI modules

- A new SAPI module named litespeed is now available.
- FastCGI support in the CGI SAPI is now always enabled and can not be disabled. See `sapi/cgi/CHANGES` for more details.
- A new CGI SAPI option, `-T`, can be used to measure repeated execution time of a script.
- CGI/FastCGI now has support for .htaccess-style user-defined `php.ini` files.
- The [dl()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.dl.html) function is now disabled by default, and is now available only under the CLI, CGI, and embed SAPIs.

# [Class and object changes in PHP 5.1, 5.0](index.md)

# [PHP 5.1](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.oop.php)

## Class and object changes

- [`instanceof`, `is_a()`, `is_subclass_of()` and `catch`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.oop.html#migration51.oop-functions)

- [Abstract private methods](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.oop.html#migration51.oop-methods)

- [Access modifiers in interfaces](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.oop.html#migration51.oop-modifiers)

- [Changes in inheritance rules](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.oop.html#migration51.oop-inheritance)

- [Class constants](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.oop.html#migration51.oop-constants)

## `instanceof`, `is_a()`, `is_subclass_of()` and `catch`

In PHP 5.0, `is_a()` was deprecated and replaced by the `instanceof` operator. There were some issues with the initial implementation of `instanceof`, which relied on `__autoload()` to search for missing classes. If the class was not present, `instanceof` would throw a fatal **`E_ERROR`** due to the failure of `__autoload()` to discover that class. The same behaviour occurred in the `catch` operator and the `is_subclass_of()` function, for the same reason.

None of these functions or operators call `__autoload()` in PHP 5.1.x, and the `class_exists()` workarounds used in code written for PHP 5.0.x, while not problematic in any way, are no longer necessary.

## Abstract private methods

Abstract private methods were supported between PHP 5.0.0 and PHP 5.0.4, but were then disallowed on the grounds that the behaviours of `private` and `abstract` are mutually exclusive.

## Access modifiers in interfaces

Under PHP 5.0, function declarations in interfaces were treated in exactly the same way as function declarations in classes. This has not been the case since October 2004, at which point only the `public` access modifier was allowed in interface function declarations. Since April 2005 - which pre-dates the PHP 5.0b1 release - the `static` modifier has also been allowed. However, the `protected` and `private` modifiers will now throw an **`E_ERROR`**, as will `abstract`. Note that this change should not affect your existing code, as none of these modifiers makes sense in the context of interfaces anyway.

## Changes in inheritance rules

Under PHP 5.0, it was possible to have a function declaration in a derived class that did not match the declaration of the same function in the base class, e.g.

This code will cause an **`E_STRICT`** error to be emitted under PHP 5.1.x.

    <?php
    class Base {
        function &return_by_ref() {
            $r = 1;
            return $r;
        }
    }

    class Derived extends Base {
        function return_by_ref() {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    ?>

## Class constants

Under PHP 5.0.x, the following code was valid:

Under PHP 5.1.x, redefinition of a class constant will throw a fatal **`E_ERROR`**.

    <?php
    class test {
        const foobar = 'foo';
        const foobar = 'bar';
    }

    ?>

# [PHP 5.0](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.oop.php)

## New Object Model

In PHP 5 there is a new Object Model. PHP's handling of objects has been completely rewritten, allowing for better performance and more features. In previous versions of PHP, objects were handled like primitive types (for instance integers and strings). The drawback of this method was that semantically the whole object was copied when a variable was assigned, or passed as a parameter to a method. In the new approach, objects are referenced by handle, and not by value (one can think of a handle as an object's identifier).

Many PHP programmers aren't even aware of the copying quirks of the old object model and, therefore, the majority of PHP applications will work out of the box, or with very few modifications.

The new Object Model is documented at the [Language Reference](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.html).

In PHP 5, function with the name of a class is called as a constructor only if defined in the same class. In PHP 4, it is called also if defined in the parent class.

See also the [zend.ze1_compatibility_mode](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.zend.ze1-compatibility-mode) directive for compatibility with PHP 4.

# [Changes to PHP Internals in PHP 5.5](index.md)

# [PHP 5.5](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration55.internals.php)

## Changes to PHP Internals

- Extensions cannot override **zend_execute()** any more and should override **zend_execute_ex()** instead. `EG(current_execute_data)` is already initialized in **zend_execute_ex()**, so for compatibility extensions may need to use `EG(current_execute_data)->prev_execute_data` instead.
- Removed `EG(arg_types_stack)`, `EX(fbc)`, `EX(called_scope)` and `EX(current_object)`.
- Added `op_array->nested_calls`, which is calculated at compile time.
- Added `EX(call_slots)`, which is an array to store information about syntaticaly nested calls (e.g. `foo(bar())`) and is preallocated together with `execute_data`.
- Added `EX(call)`, which is a pointer to a current calling function, and is an element of `EX(call_slots)`.
- Opcodes [INIT_METHOD_CALL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/internals2.opcodes.init-method-call.html), [ZEND_INIT_STATIC_METHOD_CALL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/internals2.opcodes.init-static-method-call.html), [ZEND_INIT_FCALL_BY_NAME](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/internals2.opcodes.init-fcall-by-name.html) and [ZEND_INIT_NS_FCALL_BY_NAME](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/internals2.opcodes.init-ns-fcall-by-name.html) use `result.num` as an index in `EX(call_slots)`.
- Opcode [ZEND_NEW](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/internals2.opcodes.new.html) uses `extended_value` as an index in `EX(call_slots)`.
- Opcodes [ZEND_DO_FCALL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/internals2.opcodes.do-fcall.html) and [ZEND_DO_FCALL_BY_NAME](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/internals2.opcodes.do-fcall-by-name.html) use `op2.num` as an index in `EX(call_slots)`.
- Added `op_array->used_stack`, which is calculated at compile time; the corresponding stack space is preallocated together with `execute_data`. As a result, the ZEND_SEND\* and ZEND_DO_FCALL\* opcodes no longer need to check for stack overflow.
- Removed `execute_data->Ts` field. The VM temporary variables are always allocated immediately before the `execute_data` structure, and are now accessed by their offset from the `execute_data` base pointer instead of via `execute_data->Ts`. The compiler stores new offsets in `op_array->opcodes[*].op?.num`. The **EX_TMP_VAR()** and **EX_TMP_VAR_NUM()** macros can be used to access temporary variables by offset or number. You can convert the number to an offset using **EX_TMP_VAR_NUM(0, num)** or offset to number using **(EX_TMP_VAR_NUM(0,0)-EX_TMP_VAR(0,offset))**.
- Removed the `execute_data->CVs` field. The VM compiled variables are always allocated immediately after the `execute_data` structure, and are now accessed by the offset from the `execute_data` base pointer instead of via `execute_data->CVs`. You can use the **EX_CV_NUM()** macro to access compiled variables by number.

# [Integer values in function parameters in PHP 5.1](index.md)

# [PHP 5.1](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.integer-parameters.php)

## Integer values in function parameters

With the advent of PHP 5.0.x, a new parameter parsing API was introduced which is used by a large number of PHP functions. In all versions of PHP between 5.0.x and 5.1.x, the handling of integer values was very strict and would reject non-well formed numeric values when a PHP function expected an integer. These checks have now been relaxed to support non-well formed numeric strings such as " 123" and "123 ", and will no longer fail as they did under PHP 5.0.x. However, to promote code safety and input validation, PHP functions will now emit an **`E_NOTICE`** when such strings are passed as integers.

# [Changes made to Windows support in PHP 5.3](index.md)

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.windows.php)

## Changes made to Windows support

Changes to the Windows releases:

- The minimum Windows version is now Windows XP SP3; Windows 98, ME, 2000 and NT4 are no longer supported.
- Windows binaries now target i586 and later. i386 and i486 are not supported.
- There is now experimental support for x64 versions of PHP on Windows.
- There is now compiler support for Visual C++ 9 (VC9), using Visual Studio 2008. Snapshots and releases will now also be available for VC9. Old binaries using VC6 are still supported and released in the line with VC9.
- The [PDO_OCI](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.pdo-oci.html) `php_pdo_oci8.dll` library (for use with Oracle version 8 client libraries) is no longer being built. Instead, use `php_pdo_oci.dll` (note no '8') with Oracle 10 or 11 client libraries. Connection to other database versions is still supported.
- For the [OCI8](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/book.oci8.html) extension, a new library `php_oci8_11g.dll` is available in addition to `php_oci8.dll`. Only one can be enabled at any time. Use `php_oci8.dll` with Oracle 10.2 client libraries. Use `php_oci8_11g.dll` with Oracle 11 or later client libraries. Connection to other database versions is still supported.

Windows support has been added for the following functions:

- [checkdnsrr()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.checkdnsrr.html)
- [dns_get_record()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.dns-get-record.html)
- [fnmatch()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.fnmatch.html)
- [getmxrr()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.getmxrr.html)
- [getopt()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.getopt.html)
- [imagecolorclosesthwb()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.imagecolorclosesthwb.html)
- [inet_ntop()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.inet-ntop.html)
- [inet_pton()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.inet-pton.html)
- [link()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.link.html)
- [linkinfo()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.linkinfo.html)
- [mcrypt_create_iv()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.mcrypt-create-iv.html)
- [readlink()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.readlink.html)
- [socket_create_pair()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.socket-create-pair.html) - This function was previously available on Windows, but was disabled as of PHP 4.3.0 due to a bug.
- [stream_socket_pair()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.stream-socket-pair.html)
- [symlink()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.symlink.html)
- [time_nanosleep()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.time-nanosleep.html)
- [time_sleep_until()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.time-sleep-until.html)

Other changes:

- Improved portability of the [stat()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.stat.html), [touch()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.touch.html), [filemtime()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.filemtime.html), [filesize()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.filesize.html) functions, and other related functions (100% portable for the available data).
- It is now possible to create hard links on Windows using the [link()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.link.html) function, and symbolic links using the [symlink()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.symlink.html) function. Hard links are available as of Windows 2000, and symbolic links as of Windows Vista.
- The Windows version of PHP now exposes a set of constants prefixed `PHP_WINDOWS_*`. A list of these constants and their usage can be found at [Predefined Constants](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/info.constants.html).

**Warning**

Support for the ISAPI module has been dropped. Use the improved FastCGI SAPI module instead.

> **Note**: A new dedicated site for PHP on Windows is now available, including downloads, release candidates, and snapshots in various flavors (thread-safe/not-thread-safe, VC6/VC9, x86/x64). The URL of this site is [» https://windows.php.net/](https://windows.php.net/).

# [Undeprecated features in PHP 5.3](index.md)

# [PHP 5.3](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration53.undeprecated.php)

## Undeprecated features in PHP 5.3.x

The [is_a()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.is-a.html) function has been undeprecated by popular request; it will no longer issue an **`E_STRICT`** error.

# [Error Reporting in PHP 5.2](index.md)

# [PHP 5.2](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration52.errorrep.php)

## Error Reporting

Some of the existing **`E_ERROR`** conditions have been converted to something that can be caught with a user-defined error handler. If an [**`E_RECOVERABLE_ERROR`**](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/errorfunc.constants.html) is not handled, it will behave in the same way as **`E_ERROR`** behaves in all versions of PHP. Errors of this type are logged as `Catchable fatal error`.

This change means that the value of the **`E_ALL`** [error_reporting](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/errorfunc.configuration.html#ini.error-reporting) constant is now 6143, where the previous value was 2047. Because PHP constants have no meaning outside of PHP, in some cases the integer value is used instead so these will need to be adjusted. So for example by setting the error_reporting mode from either the [httpd.conf](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/apache.configuration.html) or the `.htaccess` files, the value has to be changed accordingly. The same applies when the numeric values are used rather than the constants in PHP scripts.

As a side-effect of a change made to prevent duplicate error messages when [track_errors](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/errorfunc.configuration.html#ini.track-errors) is `On`, it is now necessary to return **`FALSE`** from user defined error handlers in order to populate [`$php_errormsg`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.phperrormsg.html). This provides a fine-grain control over the levels of messages stored.

# [Changes in SAPI Modules in PHP 7.0](index.md)

# [PHP 7.0](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration70.sapi-changes.php)

## Changes in SAPI Modules

### [FPM](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.fpm.php)

#### Unqualified [listen](https://www.php.net/manual/en/install.fpm.configuration.php#listen) ports now listen on both IPv4 and IPv6

In PHP 5, a [listen](https://www.php.net/manual/en/install.fpm.configuration.php#listen) directive with only a port number would listen on all interfaces, but only on IPv4. PHP 7 will now accept requests made via both IPv4 and IPv6.

This does not affect directives which include specific IP addresses; these will continue to only listen on that address and protocol.

# [Migrating Configuration Files in PHP 5.0](index.md)

# [PHP 5.0](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.configuration.php)

## Migrating Configuration Files

Since the ISAPI modules changed their names, from php4xxx to php5xxx, you need to make some changes in the configuration files. There were also changes in the CLI and CGI filenames. Please refer to the [corresponding section](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.cli-cgi.html) for more information.

Migrating the Apache configuration is extremely easy. See the example below to check the change you need to do:

**Example \#1 Migrating Apache configuration files for PHP 5**

``` apache-confcode
# change this line:    
LoadModule php4_module /php/sapi/php4apache2.dll

# with this one:
LoadModule php5_module /php/php5apache2.dll
```

If your web server is running PHP in CGI mode, you should note that the CGI version has changed its name from `php.exe` to `php-cgi.exe`. In Apache, you should do something like this:

**Example \#2 Migrating Apache configuration files for PHP 5, CGI mode**

``` apache-confcode
# change this line:    
Action application/x-httpd-php "/php/php.exe" 

# with this one:
Action application/x-httpd-php "/php/php-cgi.exe"
```

In other web servers you need to change either the CGI or the ISAPI module filenames.

# [Reading \[\] in PHP 5.1](index.md)

# [PHP 5.1](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.reading.php)

## Reading \[\]

    <?php
    class XmlTest {

        function test_ref(&$test) {
            $test = "ok";
        }

        function test($test) { }

        function run() {
            $ar = array();
            $this->test_ref($ar[]);
            var_dump($ar);
            $this->test($ar[]);
        }
    }

    $o = new XmlTest();
    $o->run();
    ?>

This should always have thrown a fatal **`E_ERROR`**, because \[\] cannot be used for reading in PHP. It is invalid code in PHP 4.4.2 and PHP 5.0.5 upward.

# [Changes in reference handling in PHP 5.1](index.md)

# [PHP 5.1](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.references.php)

## Changes in reference handling

- [Overview](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.references.html#migration51.references-overview)

- [Code that worked under PHP 4.3.x, but now fails](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.references.html#migration51.references-fails)

- [Code that worked under PHP 4.3.x, but now throws an error](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.references.html#migration51.references-error)

- [Code that failed under PHP 4.3.x, but now works](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.references.html#migration51.references-works)

- [Code that should have worked under PHP 5.0.x](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.references.html#migration51.references-didnotwork)

- [Warnings that came and went](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.references.html#migration51.references-warnings)

## Overview

From the PHP script writer's point of view, the change most likely to impact legacy code is in the way that references are handled in all PHP versions post-dating the PHP 4.4.0 release.

Until and including PHP 4.3, it was possible to send, assign or return variables by reference that should really be returned by value, such as a constant, a temporary value (e.g. the result of an expression), or the result of a function that had itself been returned by value, as here:

    <?php
    $foo = "123";

    function return_value() {
        global $foo;
        return $foo;
    }

    $bar = &return_value();
    ?>

Although this code would usually work as expected under PHP 4.3, in the general case the result is undefined. The Zend Engine could not act correctly on these values as references. This bug could and did lead to various hard-to-reproduce memory corruption problems, particularly where the code base was large.

In PHP 4.4.0, PHP 5.0.4 and all subsequent PHP releases, the Engine was fixed to 'know' when the reference operation is being used on a value that should not be referenced. The actual value is now used in such cases, and a warning is emitted. The warning takes the form of an **`E_NOTICE`** in PHP 4.4.0 and up, and **`E_STRICT`** in PHP 5.0.4 and up.

Code that could potentially produce memory corruption can no longer do so. However, some legacy code might work differently as a result.

## Code that worked under PHP 4.3, but now fails

    <?php
    function func(&$arraykey) {
        return $arraykey; // function returns by value!
    }

    $array = array('a', 'b', 'c');
    foreach (array_keys($array) as $key) {
        $y = &func($array[$key]);
        $z[] =& $y;
    }

    var_dump($z);
    ?>
    <

Running the above script under any version of PHP that pre-dates the reference fix would produce this output:

    array(3) {
      [0]=>
      &string(1) "a"
      [1]=>
      &string(1) "b"
      [2]=>
      &string(1) "c"
    }

Following the reference fix, the same code would result in:

    array(3) {
      [0]=>
      &string(1) "c"
      [1]=>
      &string(1) "c"
      [2]=>
      &string(1) "c"
    }

This is because, following the changes, `func()` assigns by value. The value of `$y` is re-assigned, and reference-binding is preserved from `$z`. Prior to the fix, the value was assigned by reference, leading `$y` to be re-bound on each assignment. The attempt to bind to a temporary value by reference was the cause of the memory corruption.

Such code can be made to work identically in both the pre-fix and the post-fix PHP versions. The signature of `func()` can be altered to return by reference, or the reference assignment can be removed from the result of `func()`.

    <?php
    function func() {
        return 'function return';
    }

    $x = 'original value';
    $y =& $x;
    $y = &func();
    echo $x;
    ?>

In PHP 4.3 `$x` would be 'original value', whereas after the changes it would be 'function return' - remember that where the function does not return by reference, the reference assignment is converted to a regular assignment. Again, this can be brought to a common base, either by forcing `func()` to return by reference or by eliminating the by-reference assignment.

## Code that worked under PHP 4.3.x, but now throws an error

    <?php
    class Foo {

        function getThis() {
            return $this;
        }

        function destroyThis() {
            $baz =& $this->getThis();
        }
    }

    $bar = new Foo();
    $bar->destroyThis();
    var_dump($bar);
    ?>

In PHP 5.0.3, `$bar` evaluated to **`NULL`** instead of returning an object. That happened because `getThis()` returns by value, but the value here is assigned by reference. Although it now works in the expected way, this is actually invalid code which will throw an **`E_NOTICE`** under PHP 4.4 or an **`E_STRICT`** under PHP 5.0.4 and up.

## Code that failed under PHP 4.3.x, but now works

    <?php
    function &f() {
        $x = "foo";
        var_dump($x);
        print "$x\n";
        return($a);
    }

    for ($i = 0; $i < 3; $i++) {
        $h = &f();
    }
    ?>

In PHP 4.3 the third call to [var_dump()](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/function.var-dump.html) produces **`NULL`**, due to the memory corruption caused by returning an uninitialized value by reference. This is valid code in PHP 5.0.4 and up, but threw errors in earlier releases of PHP.

    <?php
    $arr = array('a1' => array('alfa' => 'ok'));
    $arr =& $arr['a1'];
    echo '-'.$arr['alfa']."-\n";
    ?>

Until PHP 5.0.5, it wasn't possible to assign an array element by reference in this way. It now is.

## Code that `should have worked` under PHP 5.0.x

There are a couple of instances of bugs reported under PHP 5.0 prior to the reference fixes which now 'work'. However, in both cases errors are thrown by PHP 5.1.x, because the code was invalid in the first place. Returning values by reference using `self::` now works in the general case but throws an **`E_STRICT`** warning, and although your mileage may vary when assigning by reference to an overloaded object, you will still see an **`E_ERROR`** when you try it, even where the assignment itself appears to work.

## Warnings that came and went

Nested calls to functions returning by reference are valid code under both PHP 4.3.x and PHP 5.1.x, but threw an unwarranted **`E_NOTICE`** or **`E_STRICT`** under the intervening PHP releases.

    <?php
    function & foo() {
        $var = 'ok';
        return $var;
    }

    function & bar() {
        return foo();
    }

    $a =& bar();
    echo "$a\n";
    ?>

# [CLI and CGI in PHP 5.0](index.md)

# [PHP 5.0](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration5.cli-cgi.php)

## CLI and CGI

In PHP 5 there were some changes in CLI and CGI filenames. In PHP 5, the CGI version was renamed to `php-cgi.exe` (previously `php.exe`) and the CLI version now sits in the main directory (previously `cli/php.exe`).

In PHP 5 it was also introduced a new mode: `php-win.exe`. This is equal to the CLI version, except that php-win doesn't output anything and thus provides no console (no "dos box" appears on the screen). This behavior is similar to php-gtk.

In PHP 5, the CLI version will always populate the global [`$argv`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.argv.html) and [`$argc`](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/reserved.variables.argc.html) variables regardless of any `php.ini` directive setting. Even having [register_argc_argv](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ini.core.html#ini.register-argc-argv) set to `off` will have no affect in CLI.

See also the [command line reference](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/features.commandline.html).

# [OpenSSL changes in PHP 5.6](index.md)

# [PHP 5.6](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration56.openssl.php)

## OpenSSL changes in PHP 5.6.x

### Stream wrappers now verify peer certificates and host names by default when using SSL/TLS

All encrypted client streams now enable peer verification by default. By default, this will use OpenSSL's default CA bundle to verify the peer certificate. In most cases, no changes will need to be made to communicate with servers with valid SSL certificates, as distributors generally configure OpenSSL to use known good CA bundles.

The default CA bundle may be overridden on a global basis by setting either the openssl.cafile or openssl.capath configuration setting, or on a per request basis by using the [`cafile`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.cafile) or [`capath`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.capath) context options.

While not recommended in general, it is possible to disable peer certificate verification for a request by setting the [`verify_peer`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.verify-peer) context option to **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)**, and to disable peer name validation by setting the [`verify_peer_name`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.verify-peer-name) context option to **[`false`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.false)**.

### Certificate fingerprints

Support has been added for extracting and verifying certificate fingerprints. [openssl_x509_fingerprint()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-x509-fingerprint.php) has been added to extract a fingerprint from an X.509 certificate, and two [SSL stream context](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php) options have been added: `capture_peer_cert` to capture the peer's X.509 certificate, and `peer_fingerprint` to assert that the peer's certificate should match the given fingerprint.

### Default ciphers updated

The default ciphers used by PHP have been updated to a more secure list based on the [» Mozilla cipher recommendations](https://wiki.mozilla.org/Security/Server_Side_TLS#Recommended_Ciphersuite), with two additional exclusions: anonymous Diffie-Hellman ciphers, and RC4.

This list can be accessed via the new **[`OPENSSL_DEFAULT_STREAM_CIPHERS`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/openssl.ciphers.php#constant.openssl-default-stream-ciphers)** constant, and can be overridden (as in previous PHP versions) by setting the [`ciphers`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.ciphers) context option.

### Compression disabled by default

SSL/TLS compression has been disabled by default to mitigate the CRIME attack. PHP 5.4.13 added a [`disable_compression`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/context.ssl.php#context.ssl.disable-compression) context option to allow compression to be disabled: this is now set to **[`true`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.true)** (that is, compression is disabled) by default.

### Allow servers to prefer their cipher order

The `honor_cipher_order` SSL context option has been added to allow encrypted stream servers to mitigate BEAST vulnerabilities by preferring the server's ciphers to the client's.

### Access the negotiated protocol and cipher

The protocol and cipher that were negotiated for an encrypted stream can now be accessed via [stream_get_meta_data()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-get-meta-data.php) or [stream_context_get_options()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-context-get-options.php) when the `capture_session_meta` SSL context option is set to **[`true`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.true)**.

```
<?php
$ctx = stream_context_create(['ssl' => [
    'capture_session_meta' => TRUE
]]);
 
$html = file_get_contents('https://google.com/', FALSE, $ctx);
$meta = stream_context_get_options($ctx)['ssl']['session_meta'];
var_dump($meta);
?>
```

The above example will output:

    array(4) {
      ["protocol"]=>
      string(5) "TLSv1"
      ["cipher_name"]=>
      string(20) "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA"
      ["cipher_bits"]=>
      int(128)
      ["cipher_version"]=>
      string(11) "TLSv1/SSLv3"
    }

### New options for perfect forward secrecy in encrypted stream servers

Encrypted client streams already support perfect forward secrecy, as it is generally controlled by the server. PHP encrypted server streams using certificates capable of perfect forward secrecy do not need to take any additional action to enable PFS; however a number of new SSL context options have been added to allow more control over PFS and deal with any compatibility issues that may arise.

`ecdh_curve`  
This option allows the selection of a specific curve for use with ECDH ciphers. If not specified, `prime256v1` will be used.

`dh_param`  
A path to a file containing parameters for Diffie-Hellman key exchange, such as that created by the following command:

``` shellcode
openssl dhparam -out /path/to/my/certs/dh-2048.pem 2048
```

`single_dh_use`  
If set to **[`true`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.true)**, a new key pair will be created when using Diffie-Hellman parameters, thereby improving forward secrecy.

`single_ecdh_use`  
If set to **[`true`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.constants.php#constant.true)**, a new key pair will always be generated when ECDH cipher suites are negotiated. This improves forward secrecy.

### SSL/TLS version selection

It is now possible to select specific versions of SSL and TLS via the `crypto_method` SSL context option or by specifying a specific transport when creating a stream wrapper (for example, by calling [stream_socket_client()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-socket-client.php) or [stream_socket_server()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-socket-server.php)).

The `crypto_method` SSL context option accepts a bitmask enumerating the protocols that are permitted, as does the `crypto_type` of [stream_socket_enable_crypto()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.stream-socket-enable-crypto.php).

| Protocol(s) | Client flag | Server flag | Transport |
|----|----|----|----|
| Any TLS or SSL version | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_ANY_CLIENT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-any-client)** | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_ANY_SERVER`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-any-server)** | `ssl://` |
| Any TLS version | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_CLIENT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tls-client)** | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_SERVER`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tls-server)** | `tls://` |
| TLS 1.0 | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_0_CLIENT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tlsv1-0-client)** | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_0_SERVER`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tlsv1-0-server)** | `tlsv1.0://` |
| TLS 1.1 | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_1_CLIENT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tlsv1-1-client)** | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_1_SERVER`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tlsv1-1-server)** | `tlsv1.1://` |
| TLS 1.2 | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_2_CLIENT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tlsv1-2-client)** | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_2_SERVER`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-tlsv1-2-server)** | `tlsv1.2://` |
| SSL 3 | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv3_CLIENT`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-sslv3-client)** | **[`STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv3_SERVER`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/stream.constants.php#constant.stream-crypto-method-sslv3-server)** | `sslv3://` |

**Selected protocol versions and corresponding options**

```
<?php

// Requiring TLS 1.0 or better when using file_get_contents():
$ctx = stream_context_create([
    'ssl' => [
        'crypto_method' => STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_CLIENT,
    ],
]);
$html = file_get_contents('https://google.com/', false, $ctx);

// Requiring TLS 1.1 or 1.2:
$ctx = stream_context_create([
    'ssl' => [
        'crypto_method' => STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_1_CLIENT |
                           STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_2_CLIENT,
    ],
]);
$html = file_get_contents('https://google.com/', false, $ctx);

// Connecting using the tlsv1.2:// stream socket transport.
$sock = stream_socket_client('tlsv1.2://google.com:443/');

?>
```

### [openssl_get_cert_locations()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-get-cert-locations.php) added

The [openssl_get_cert_locations()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-get-cert-locations.php) function has been added: it returns the default locations PHP will search when looking for CA bundles.

```
<?php
var_dump(openssl_get_cert_locations());
?>
```

The above example will output:

    array(8) {
      ["default_cert_file"]=>
      string(21) "/etc/pki/tls/cert.pem"
      ["default_cert_file_env"]=>
      string(13) "SSL_CERT_FILE"
      ["default_cert_dir"]=>
      string(18) "/etc/pki/tls/certs"
      ["default_cert_dir_env"]=>
      string(12) "SSL_CERT_DIR"
      ["default_private_dir"]=>
      string(20) "/etc/pki/tls/private"
      ["default_default_cert_area"]=>
      string(12) "/etc/pki/tls"
      ["ini_cafile"]=>
      string(0) ""
      ["ini_capath"]=>
      string(0) ""
    }

### SPKI support

Support has been added for generating, extracting and verifying signed public key and challenges (SPKAC). [openssl_spki_new()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-spki-new.php), [openssl_spki_verify()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-spki-verify.php), [openssl_spki_export_challenge()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-spki-export-challenge.php), and [openssl_spki_export()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.openssl-spki-export.php) have been added to create, verify export PEM public key and associated challenge from SPKAC's generated from a `KeyGen` HTML5 element.

`openssl_spki_new`  
Generates a new SPKAC using private key, challenge string and hashing algorithm.

```
<?php
$pkey = openssl_pkey_new();
openssl_pkey_export($pkey, 'secret passphrase');

$spkac = openssl_spki_new($pkey, 'challenge string');
?>
```

The above example will output:

    

`openssl_spki_verify`  
Verifies provided SPKAC.

```
<?php
$pkey = openssl_pkey_new();
openssl_pkey_export($pkey, 'secret passphrase');

$spkac = openssl_spki_new($pkey, 'challenge string');
var_dump(openssl_spki_verify($spkac));
?>
```

`openssl_spki_export_challenge`  
Exports associated challenge from provided SPKAC.

```
<?php
$pkey = openssl_pkey_new();
openssl_pkey_export($pkey, 'secret passphrase');

$spkac = openssl_spki_new($pkey, 'challenge string');
$challenge = openssl_spki_export_challenge($spkac);
echo $challenge;
?>
```

The above example will output:

    challenge string

`openssl_spki_export`  
Exports the PEM formatted RSA public key from SPKAC.

```
<?php
$pkey = openssl_pkey_new();
openssl_pkey_export($pkey, 'secret passphrase');

$spkac = openssl_spki_new($pkey, 'challenge string');
echo openssl_spki_export($spkac);
?>
```

The above example will output:

    -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
    MIGfMA0GCSqGSIb3DQEBAQUAA4GNADCBiQKBgQDcvQh9SKOPv4DwI8LwSaFx02h7
    l9QCiDs6sF2GfsSTEUG61SnjQ/v4uJiLKBgbVOagj9rkSCwtTez23ATPeGaBj2Zg
    ipv+tv5IXyqUP8ropXJQ5ELtbXPUN/gvw7cO5EbPHr/7eMhbpw8Gl+AfWxW5hLW8
    MGw/+AwwjHBOwong/QIDAQAB
    -----END PUBLIC KEY-----

# [Checking for E_STRICT in PHP 5.1](index.md)

# [PHP 5.1](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration51.errorcheck.php)

## Checking for **`E_STRICT`**

If you only have a single script to check, you can pick up **`E_STRICT`** errors using PHP's commandline lint facility:

``` shellcode
php -d error_reporting=4095 -l script_to_check.php
```

For larger projects, the shell script below will achieve the same task:

``` shellcode
#!/bin/sh

directory=$1

shift

# These extensions are checked
extensions="php inc"

check_file ()
{
  echo -ne "Doing PHP syntax check on $1 ..."

  # Options:
  ERRORS=`/www/php/bin/php -d display_errors=1 -d html_errors=0 -d error_prepend_string=" " -d error_append_string=" " -d error_reporting=4095 -l $1 | grep -v "No syntax errors detected"`

  if test -z "$ERRORS"; then
    echo -ne "OK."
  else
    echo -e "Errors found!\n$ERRORS"
  fi

  echo
}

# loop over remaining file args
for FILE in "$@" ; do
  for ext in $extensions; do
     if echo $FILE | grep "\.$ext$" > /dev/null; then
       if test -f $FILE; then
         check_file "$FILE"
       fi
     fi
  done
done
```

# [New Error Messages in PHP 5.2](index.md)

# [PHP 5.2](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/migration52.error-messages.php)

## New Error Messages

Below are the new error messages that have not been discussed elsewhere in this document.

**Example \#1 In PHP Core**

    <?php
    echo " ";
    session_regenerate_id();
    /*  Warning:  session_regenerate_id(): Cannot regenerate
        session id - headers already sent in filename on line n */

    str_word_count("string", 4);
    /* Warning:  str_word_count(): Invalid format value 4
       in filename on line n */

    strripos("foo", "f", 4);
    /* Notice:  strripos(): Offset is greater than the
       length of haystack string in filename on line n */

    strrpos("foo", "f", 4);
    /* Notice:  strrpos(): Offset is greater than the
       length of haystack string in filename on line n */

    /* As of PHP 5.2.1, when allow_url_include is OFF (default) */
    include "php://input";
    /* Warning:  include(): URL file-access is disabled
       in the server configuration in filename on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#2 [Object Oriented Code](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/language.oop5.html) in PHP Core**

    <?php
    interface foo {
    }
    class bar implements foo, foo {
    }
    /* Fatal error: Class bar cannot implement previously
       implemented interface foo in filename on line n */


    class foo {
        public $bar;
        function __get($var)
        {
            return $this->bar;
        }
    }

    $foo = new foo;
    $bar =& $foo->prop;
    /* Notice: Indirect modification of overloaded property
       foo::$prop has no effect in filename on line n */


    class foo implements iterator {
        public function current() {
        }
        public function next() {
        }
        public function key() {
        }
        public function valid() {
        }
        public function rewind() {
        }
    }

    $foo = new foo();
    foreach($foo as &$ref) {}
    /* Fatal error: An iterator cannot be used with foreach
       by reference in filename on line n */


    class foo {
        private function __construct() {
        }
    }
    class bar extends foo {
        public function __construct() {
            parent::__construct();
            /* Fatal error:  Cannot call private
               foo::__construct() in filename on line n */
        }
    }
    new bar;


    stream_filter_register("", "class");
    /* Warning:  stream_filter_register(): Filter name
       cannot be empty in filename on line n */


    stream_filter_register("filter", "");
    /* Warning:  stream_filter_register(): Class name
       cannot be empty in filename on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#3 In the [bzip2](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.bzip2.html) Extension**

    <?php
    bzopen("", "w");
    /* Warning:  bzopen(): filename cannot be empty
       in filename on line n */

    bzopen("foo", "a");
    /* Warning:  bzopen(): 'a' is not a valid mode for
       bzopen(). Only 'w' and 'r' are supported in
       filename on line n */

    $fp = fopen("foo", "w");
    bzopen($fp, "r");
    /* Warning:  bzopen(): cannot read from a stream
       opened in write only mode in filename on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#4 In the [datetime](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.datetime.html) Extension**

    <?php
    strtotime("today", "now");
    /* Warning:  strtotime() expects parameter 2 to be
       long, string given in filename on line n */

    /* As of PHP 5.2.1 */
    new DateTime(new stdclass);
    /* Fatal error: Uncaught exception 'Exception' with
       message 'DateTime::__construct() expects parameter
       1 to be string, object given' in filename:n */
    ?>

**Example \#5 In the [dBase](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.dbase.html) Extension**

    <?php
    dbase_open("foo", -1);
    /* Warning: Invalid access mode -1 in filename on line n */

    /* As of PHP 5.2.1 */
    dbase_open("foo", null);
    /* Warning: The filename cannot be empty in filename on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#6 In the [mcrypt](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.mcrypt.html) Extension**

    <?php
    $key = "this is a secret key";
    $td = mcrypt_module_open('tripledes', '', 'ecb', '');
    $iv = mcrypt_create_iv (mcrypt_enc_get_iv_size($td),
                            MCRYPT_RAND);
    mcrypt_generic_init($td, $key, $iv);
    $encrypted_data = mcrypt_generic($td, "");
    /* Warning: mcrypt_generic(): An empty string was
       passed in filename on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#7 In the [oci8](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.oci8.html) Extension**

    <?php
    oci_connect("user", "pass", "db", "bogus_charset");
    /* Warning: Invalid character set name:
       bogus_charset in filename on line n */

    $oci = oci_connect("user", "pass", "db");
    oci_password_change($oci, "", "old", "new");
    /* Warning: username cannot be empty in filename
       on line n */

    oci_password_change($oci, "user", "", "new");
    /* Warning: old password cannot be empty in filename
       on line n */

    oci_password_change($oci, "user", "old", "");
    /* Warning: new password cannot be empty in filename
       on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#8 In the [SPL](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.spl.html) Extension**

    <?php
    $obj = new SplFileObject(__FILE__);
    $obj->fgetcsv("foo");
    /* Warning:  SplFileObject::fgetcsv(): delimiter must
       be a character in filename on line n */

    $obj->fgetcsv(",", "foo");
    /* Warning:  SplFileObject::fgetcsv(): enclosure must
       be a character in filename on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#9 In the [Semaphore](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.sem.html) (sysvmsg) extension**

    <?php
    /* Warning:  maximum size of the message has to be
       greater then zero in filename on line n */
    ?>

**Example \#10 A 5.2.1+ [Zip](https://php-legacy-docs.zend.com/manual/php5/en/ref.zip.html) Example**

    <?php
    $obj = new ZipArchive();
    $obj->open('archive.zip');
    $obj->setCommentName('', 'comment');
    /* Notice:  ZipArchive::setCommentName(): Empty string
       as entry name in filename on line n */

    /* As of PHP 5.2.1 */
    $obj->getCommentName('');
    /* Notice:  ZipArchive::getCommentName(): Empty string
       as entry name in filename on line n */
    ?>
